content:
谷歌前首席执行官埃里克·施密特创立的智囊团的一份新报告量化了美国国防工业基地在关键稀土矿物方面依赖中国的严峻现实。它还详细说明了如果这种微妙的供应关系破裂，哪些武器系统可能面临最大的影响。这份白皮书专门从特别竞争研究项目中获得，利用供应链科技公司 Exiger 的人工智能情报来评估有多少由国家物品识别号 (NIIN) 识别的独特组件含有关键矿物质，例如锑、镓、锗和钨。美国的武器库依赖于稀土的稳定供应，尤其是最先进的武器。美国空军 摄影：Tech Sgt.托马斯·巴利科技。中士。 Thomas Barley 通过对近 900 万个零件和 3,000 个美国军用武器系统的评估，该公司在 1,400 个武器系统中发现了 28,000 多个独特部件仅含有这四种稀土。由于近期的危机，这些部分的隔离尤其重要：中国出口管制的暂停将于 11 月到期。根据白皮书，武器部署计划以及战备和保障活动很有可能受到干扰。然而，Exiger 首席战略和全球事务官基特·康克林 (Kit Conklin) 表示，危机已经到来。
在接受 TWZ 采访时，他指出日本正面临着生产停顿的前景，因为今年早些时候中国切断了一些稀土供应超过 80%。康克林表示：“毫无疑问，目前对于许多试图获得中国批准的许可证但没有获得许可证的公司来说，这是一场危机。” “因此，当前的生产存在真正的风险，当我考虑我们的生产和规模扩张时，无论是无人机工业基地还是试图将我们的拦截器产能扩大到每年 1,000、2,000、3,000 个拦截器，我的意思是，这些都是我们面临的真正的瓶颈，正在影响我们现在向作战人员提供这些拦截器的能力。”数据显示，供应链和制造中断风险最大的武器系统之一是至关重要的弗吉尼亚级潜艇，它需要 300 多个含有四种元素的关键 NIIN，其中包括 190 个需要锗的部件。弗吉尼亚号（SSN 774）是弗吉尼亚级的领舰，是美国海军快速攻击潜艇部队的骨干力量。美国海军照片由通用动力电船公司拍摄 美国海军锗是锌矿石的副产品，用于光学、夜视系统、EO/IR 设备等。一月份，五角大楼宣布投资 1800 万美元建设位于圣路易斯的美国唯一的锗生产设施。
犹他州乔治市将在未具体说明的期限内将炼油能力扩大“七倍”，达到每年 20 吨以上。中国控制着全球约 68% 的精炼锗。它对用于半导体和太阳能电池，尤其是先进雷达的镓的控制力要大得多，控制着高达 99% 的产量。每艘弗吉尼亚级潜艇都需要 50 个含有镓的独特部件。中国控制着大约一半的锑产量，用于硬化弹药以及制造光学和电子产品；高达80%的钨供应量，用于制造工具、弹头和耐热部件。虽然它这样做

【原文 English Original】
A new report from the think tank founded by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt quantifies the grim realities of the U.S. defense industrial base’s dependence on China for critical rare earth minerals. It also details which weapons systems might face the most impact if that delicate supply relationship breaks down. The white paper, exclusively obtained from the Special Competitive Studies Project, uses AI intelligence from the supply chain tech firm Exiger to assess how many unique components, identified by National Item Identification Number, or NIIN, contain critical minerals, such as antimony, gallium, germanium and tungsten. America’s arsenal depends on a steady flow of rare earths, and especially its most advanced weapons. U.S. Air Force photo by Tech Sgt. Thomas Barley Tech. Sgt. Thomas Barley From an assessment of almost nine million parts and 3,000 U.S. military weapon systems, the company identified more than 28,000 unique components across 1,400 weapons systems containing just these four rare earths. The isolation of these parts is relevant in particular because of a near-term crisis: the expiration of a suspension on Chinese export controls set to take effect in November. Disruption to weapons fielding plans, as well as operational readiness and sustainment activities, according to the white paper, is very much a possibility. Yet according to Kit Conklin, chief strategy and global affairs officer at Exiger, the crisis is already here. In an interview with TWZ , he pointed to Japan, which is facing the prospect of a manufacturing halt after China choked off supply of some rare earths to the tune of more than 80% earlier this year. “There’s no question that right now it’s a crisis for a lot of companies that are trying to get licenses approved by China and just not getting the licenses,” Conklin said. “So there’s real risk to current production, and when I think about us and scaling, whether it’s the drone industrial base or trying to scale our interceptor capacity to 1,000, 2,000, 3,000 interceptors a year, I mean, these are real choke points that we have that are impacting our ability to deliver these to the warfighter right now.” Among the weapons systems most at risk for supply chain and manufacturing disruption, according to the data, is the vital Virginia -class submarine, which requires more than 300 critical NIINs containing the four elements, including 190 parts requiring germanium. USS Virginia (SSN 774), the leader of the Virginia class that serves as the backbone of the U.S. Navy’s fast attack submarine force. U.S. Navy photo by General Dynamics Electric Boat U.S. Navy Germanium, used in optics, night vision systems, EO/IR equipment and more, is a byproduct of zinc ore . In January, the Pentagon announced an $18 million investment in the country’s only germanium production facility in St. George, Utah to expand refining capacity “sevenfold” to more than 20 metric tons annually by an unspecified deadline. China controls some 68% of the world’s refined germanium. It has a far greater chokehold on gallium, used in semiconductors and solar cells, and especially advanced radars, controlling up to 99% of production . Each Virginia -class sub requires 50 unique parts containing gallium. China controls about half the production of antimony, used to harden ammunition and to manufacture optics and electronics; and up to 80% of the supply of tungsten, used in manufacturing tools, warheads and heat-resistant components. While it doesn’t break down components by weight, the report notes that the rare earth requirements for the Virginia -class sub are also considerable by mass: each sub required 9,200 pounds of the elements, while an F-35 Joint Strike Fighter jet requires 900 pounds. Special Competitive Studies Project The Virginia -class submarine is America’s only in-production fast-attack nuclear-powered sub that has been in service since 2004. Twenty three of these critical vessels are in service today , or roughly half of the total planned program, with the remaining boats yet to be built. It’s notable in the context of the paper because it has multiple points of exposure to supply chain disruption. Another of these exposure points: its 1,700 mission or safety-critical parts requiring casting, forging or extrusion. As the report lays out, supply chain bottlenecks around limited metal casting, forging and extruding capacity are delaying production timelines and putting manufacturing at risk. China, again, produces about half of the world’s casting output and “is often the sole option for large castings,” the paper found. The analysis shows that more than half, or nearly 8,000, unique supply items containing steel castings have delivery lead times of more than 36 weeks. More than 9,400 items containing extruded aluminum, about 47% of these parts, have lead times that long. A large metal casting for a port crane. Voestalpine Foundry Group “ Virginia -class submarines, already threatened by U.S. reliance on China for critical minerals, are reportedly also three years behind schedule, potentially due in part to the lack of domestic large-scale casting capacity,” the report finds. An analysis of Navy construction timelines published earlier this year does indeed find that 10 of the 12 Virginia subs now under construction face delays of 36-44 months. Alarmingly, a recent war game simulation found that the U.S. could not replace ships, planes and missiles lost to combat specifically due to casting and forging shortfalls, the report notes. That’s despite a $2 billion Pentagon initiative launched in 2024 aimed at revitalizing this industry. Beyond submarines, the report shows that aircraft, including some of the nation’s workhorse fighter jets, face outsized production and sustainment risk due to rare-earth elements and casting/forging dependencies. The B-2 Spirit bomber – the nation’s only nuclear-armed stealth bomber until fielding begins on the B-21 Raider sometime next year – requires 782 parts containing the four rare-earth elements isolated in the report. Special Competitive Studies Project The F/A-18 Hornet family of fighters flown by the Navy and Marine Corps, including the Navy’s Growler electronic warfare variant, tops the list for dependency on steel castings, with 3,800 individual parts requiring the process. Following is the KC-135 Stratotanker, with 2,570 parts. All 10 of the systems requiring the most metal castings for production are aircraft, the analysis shows. The legacy Hornet and the KC-135 have been out of production for decades, while the Navy’s Super Hornet will see its production line go cold in 2027. Any ongoing demand for castings for these systems would thus be in spares and repair parts.  Special Competitive Studies Project Military aircraft also represent the highest-need category among weapons systems requiring cadmium plating, a process used to make aerospace components corrosion-resistant.  The domestic supplier base has shrunk due to EPA safety limitations established in 2008. All of the top 10 weapons systems requiring the most cadmium-plated parts are aircraft, with the KC-135 topping the list with 2,780 unique components. The C-130 Hercules transport, B-52 Stratofortress bomber and Galaxy C-5 transport all have more than 2,000 parts. Special Competitive Studies Project The B-52, which is undergoing a service life extension to take it into the 2050s – past its century mark – may run into modernization delays not only over cadmium-plated and steel-casted components, but also due to overly rigid military specifications, which increase lead time and delays. The white paper cites the bomber’s rib airfoil and fuel vent valve components, which both have lead times of more than 400 days due in part to production being burdened with dozens of mil-spec compliance requirements, which the authors say have not kept pace with today’s commercial practices. “The requirement for a part to meet so many mil-specs, if not reasonably necessary, may limit the number of possible suppliers of that part, potentially increasing its lead time and bottlenecking production,” they write. “For the B-52, this could inhibit current modernization efforts intended to keep the airplane operational through the 2050s.” A B-52H Stratofortress undergoing programmed depot maintenance is towed into a hangar at Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma, July 28, 2025. U.S. Air Force photo by Paul Shirk Paul Shirk A final risk the paper addresses is workforce shortages and dangers from limited suppliers creating single points of failure. Across defense, the number of small suppliers has decreased by 43% in the last decade, it notes. It cites, as a case study, the February 2025 fire that forced the closure of SPS Technologies in Jenkintown, Penn. – a fastener maker that produced components for more than 1,000 weapons systems and was deemed critical for 90, including the Nimitz -class carrier, the F/A-18 fighter and the M1 Abrams tank. For systems including the Tomahawk Land Attack Missile and the MH-60 Black Hawk helicopter, the facility was a single-source supplier. With operations offline until at least 2028, the supply chain has been “actively disrupted” due to the outage of just one facility, according to the paper. “This case underscores the risk of single sourcing in the defense industrial base and the need to qualify alternate sources to avoid such significant chokepoints,” the authors write. The paper hails work that has already begun to invest in domestic critical minerals production and shore up the defense industrial base. But it does hint that these efforts may be too late to avoid a crash if China shuts off or severely reduces exports. The paper notes that, on average, it takes the U.S. 29 years to open a new mine. The U.S. has one established domestic mine: The Mountain Pass Rare Earth Mine and Processing Facility, just outside of Las Vegas. Initially established in 1952 and reopened in 2018 after a long hiatus, it now produces more than 50,000 tons of rare earth oxides annually . Last year, for the first time in seven decades, a new domestic rare-earth mine opened in Wyoming , stating plans to start producing ores extracted from coal, including gallium and germanium, by 2029 . Production is projected to total 456 tons of rare earths per year. The project had been in development for more than a decade before opening.  The Mountain Pass Rare Earth Mine and Processing Facility. MP Materials Conklin said a July executive order aimed at developing domestic production of rare earths while collecting data on what elements systems required created opportunities for smart policy creation – perhaps in the next National Defense Authorization Act – around holistically attacking the problem.  “I would love for us to figure out a way to get out of thinking about these supply chain risks system by system. We tend to have disparate requirements to look at the nuclear triad or subs or interceptors,” he said. “I think with the executive order that came out earlier this year, there’s a real opportunity for Congress to legislate on some of these issues beyond just figuring out what the risk [is] for antimony in the sub industrial base, and thinking about it a little bit more holistically.” One potential solution he proposed: an agency within the executive branch (led, perhaps, by a critical minerals czar) who can coordinate production needs and resourcing and develop the most efficient pathways to secure needed materials. There are few weapons that are not impacted by the scarcity of robust sources for rare earths. RTX While no U.S. defense manufacturer has yet publicly cited manufacturing disruptions due to rare earth availability, signs are increasing that the federal government is taking supply concerns seriously. In addition to Project Vault , a $12 billion White House initiative announced in February that would create a strategic stockpile of rare earths akin to existing stockpiles of critical medical supplies and petroleum, the U.S. Army has begun extending long-term leases on military land to companies seeking to build critical mineral processing facilities. Conklin said he doesn’t anticipate major changes in rare earth exports between now and the end of the year, describing the U.S.-China supply relationship as “in a bit of a détente.” That said, with new policies pending, we could be only days away from new revelations about the extent of the impact of these materials on the defense manufacturing enterprise. Contact the editor: Tyler@twz.com The post These Are The U.S. Weapons Most At Risk In The Looming Rare Earths Supply Crisis appeared first on TWZ .

summary: 美国海军陆战队下士2026 年 8 月 25 日，在菲律宾博赫多尔举行的群岛海岸防御连续体 26.4 期间，第一海军陆战队远征军东南亚海军陆战队轮换部队北部海空炮火联络连分遣队的一名火力支援海军陆战队员与菲律宾海军陆战队第四海军旅一起进行火力支援小组训练。该服务上周宣布，东南亚轮换力量目前正在第二次连续轮换到菲律宾。 MRF-SEA 于 10 月 26 日进行了轮换营业额。 MR
content:
美国海军陆战队下士2026 年 8 月 25 日，在菲律宾博赫多尔举行的群岛海岸防御连续体 26.4 期间，第一海军陆战队远征军东南亚海军陆战队轮换部队北部海空炮火联络连分遣队的一名火力支援海军陆战队员与菲律宾海军陆战队第四海军旅一起进行火力支援小组训练。该服务上周宣布，东南亚轮换力量目前正在第二次连续轮换到菲律宾。 MRF-SEA 于 10 月 26 日进行了轮换。MRF-SEA 最初是一支为期六个月的轮换部队，从 10 月到 3 月部署到该地区，但其任务在 4 月延长。应菲律宾政府邀请，该部队目前在菲律宾持续驻扎，以继续与菲律宾军方合作。 MRF-SEA 是在第一海军陆战队远征军支持下作战的两支轮换部队之一，另一支是海军陆战队轮换部队-达尔文。与作为海军陆战队空地特遣部队部署的 MRF-D 不同，MRF-SEA 部署为可扩展的特遣部队，其指挥总部是常设组成部分。其他海军陆战队单位将根据需要进行分配。我们。
2026 年 6 月 24 日，为支持 MRF-SEA 而部署的第三濒海战斗队、海军陆战队第三临海团、海军陆战队第三师的海军陆战队士兵和海军陆战队第四旅的菲律宾海军陆战队士兵，在菲律宾巴丹群岛伊特巴亚特的海上关键地形安全行动期间，在地形巡逻的同时参加城市地形军事行动，以支持 KAMANDAG 10。美国海军陆战队照片轮换前延期后，MRF-SEA 的指挥部门将根据预定活动的地点在东南亚国家之间移动。自四月份以来，指挥部门一直驻扎在菲律宾。目前的部署是 MRF-SEA 的第六次迭代。轮换部署于 2022 年开始。根据海军陆战队的一份新闻稿，该部队的存在旨在加强联合战备和美菲联盟，每次轮换都建立在之前部队的关系和经验教训的基础上，MRF-SEA 称之为“有目的的存在”。 “我们的目标从来都不是简单地出现在菲律宾，”即将卸任的 MRF-SEA 轮换指挥官罗伯特·邦恩 (Robert Bunn) 上校说。 “存在必须有目的。与我们的菲律宾盟友一起进行的每一次演习、计划会议和重复都是一个机会，让我们变得更加具有互操作性、响应能力和能力，并在每次活动中逐渐变得更好。
下一次轮换现在有机会吸取这些教训和关系，推动联盟向前迈进一步。”之前的 MRF-SEA 轮换中，该部队在“肩并肩 26”演习、“卡曼达格 10”演习以及通过群岛海岸防御连续体 (ACDC) 进行的一系列双边活动期间与菲律宾军队一起进行了训练。该连续体在主要演习之间提供了反复训练，使美国和菲律宾部队能够将一次活动中的经验教训应用到下一次活动中。 ACDC是一系列双边训练活动和主题专家交流，支持菲律宾海军陆战队的现代化努力和菲律宾海军陆战队的群岛海岸防御概念，同时加强美国和菲律宾军队之间的联合战备。

U.S. Marine Corps Cpl. Antwon Brooks, a fire support Marine with Air Naval Gunfire Liaison Company Detachment – North, Marine Rotational Force – Southeast Asia, I Marine Expeditionary Force, conducts fire support team training alongside Philippine marines with 4th Marine Brigade, Philippine Marine Corps, during Archipelagic Coastal Defense Continuum 26.4 in Bojeador, Philippines, Aug. 25, 2026. US Marine Corps photo Marine Rotational Force-Southeast Asia is now on its second continuous rotation to the Philippines, the service announced last week. MRF-SEA held a rotation turnover on Oct. 26. MRF-SEA originally began as a six-month rotational force that deployed to the region from October to March but its mission was extended in April . The force is now providing a continuous presence in the Philippines at the invitation of the country’s government to continue cooperation with its military. MRF-SEA is one of two rotational forces operating under the aegis of I Marine Expeditionary Force, with the other being Marine Rotational Force-Darwin. Unlike MRF-D, which deploys as a Marine Air-Ground Task Force, MRF-SEA deploys as a scalable task force with its command headquarters being the permanent component. Other Marine units are assigned as and when required. U.S. Marines assigned to 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, which deployed to support MRF-SEA, and Philippine marines assigned to 4th Marine Brigade, patrol through terrain while participating in military operations in urban terrain training during maritime key terrain security operations in support of KAMANDAG 10 at Itbayat, Batanes islands, Philippines, June 24, 2026. US Marine Corps photo Before the rotation extension, the command element of the MRF-SEA would move between Southeast Asian countries based on where scheduled activities would take place. Since April, the command element has been based in the Philippines The current deployment is the sixth iteration of MRF-SEA. The rotational deployment began in 2022. The unit’s presence is designed to strengthen combined readiness and the U.S.-Philippine Alliance, according to a Marine Corps news release, with each rotation building on the relationships and lessons of the force before in an approach MRF-SEA calls “presence with purpose.” “Our goal was never simply to be present in the Philippines,” said Col. Robert Bunn, commanding officer of the outgoing MRF-SEA rotation. “Presence has to have purpose. Every exercise, planning session and repetition alongside our Philippine allies was an opportunity to become more interoperable, responsive and capable together, progressively getting better with each event. The next rotation now has the opportunity to take those lessons and relationships to move the alliance another step forward.” The previous rotation of MRF-SEA saw the force train alongside Philippine troops during Balikatan 26, KAMANDAG 10 and a series of bilateral events through the Archipelagic Coastal Defense Continuum (ACDC). The continuum provided recurring training between major exercises, allowing U.S. and Philippine forces to apply lessons from one event to the next. ACDC is is a series of bilateral training activities and subject matter expert exchanges that support Philippine Marine Corps modernization efforts and the Philippine Marine Corps’ Archipelagic Coastal Defense Concept along with strengthening combined readiness between U.S. and Philippine forces Training throughout the previous MRF-SEA rotation included command and control, sensing, fires integration, maritime domain awareness, aviation, communications and unmanned systems. Marines also tested how forces and equipment could move, communicate and operate across the Philippines’ distributed and archipelagic terrain. This included testing the mobility of the AN/TPS-80 Ground/Air Task-Oriented Radar as part of ACDC training and movement of the Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System (NMESIS) and Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) from ports to distributed exercise locations as part of KAMANDAG 10. U.S. Marines assigned to 3rd Littoral Anti-Air Battalion, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, drive a Marine Air Defense Integrated System off a Philippine surface connector in support of maritime key terrain security operations during KAMANDAG 10 at Calayan, Philippines, June 22, 2026. US Marine Corps photo The incoming rotation will continue the progression of the U.S.-Philippine partnership through ACDC and Exercise Balikatan 27, according to the release. Training will continue to focus on operating across distributed and archipelagic terrain, strengthening the ability of U.S. and Philippine forces to coordinate, maneuver and sustain operations across geographically dispersed locations. Marines and sailors will also continue bilateral humanitarian assistance, disaster response and crisis response training. “Our Marines and sailors are inheriting more than a mission, they are inheriting momentum,” said Col. Coby Moran, commanding officer of the incoming MRF-SEA rotation. “We will build on the relationships, lessons and interoperability developed by the Marines and sailors before us and continue working shoulder-to-shoulder with our Philippine allies.” Moran previously operated in the Philippines, leading a I MEF technical assistance and advisory team in April that oversaw a maritime prepositioning force offload at the Port of Cagayan de Oro, Mindanao, Philippines. The event was the first MPF offload at Mindanao, according to a Marine Corps news release at the time . The offload saw roll-on/roll-off cargo ship USNS Sgt. William W. Seay (T-AKR-302) transport vehicles and equipment to I MEF, which was preparing for Exercise Balikatan 26 in the Philippines. “MPF operations are a unique capability of the Marine Corps,” said Moran in the release. “They allow us to deliver capabilities anywhere in the world, providing critical combat power to Marine air-ground task force commanders.” The Marine Corps has not disclosed whether MRF-SEA will now only focus on the Philippines or whether it will continue leading Marine Corps engagement and activities with other countries in the region alongside its activities in the Philippines.

content:
没有研究表明中国的宣传或虚假信息在中期选举中发挥了关键作用，特别是与俄罗斯的侵略性尝试相比。然而，存在重大盲点。如果愿意的话，北京完全有能力通过微信应用程序和中国的人工智能模型来塑造政治辩论。北京的目标可能不是转移对国会的控制权，而是减少已知的共产党批评者的存在，特别是那些在国会及行政部门中国委员会任职的人。该委员会由国会于 2000 年 10 月成立，负责监督中国的人权和法治。委员会成员参加了几场竞争激烈的竞选，其中包括俄亥俄州前参议员谢罗德·布朗和阿拉斯加现任委员会主席丹·沙利文。爱荷华州和弗吉尼亚州的众议院竞选涉及现任委员会成员扎克·纳恩和珍·基甘斯。正在竞选爱荷华州参议员的阿什利·辛森 (Ashley Hinson) 是众议院中国共产党特别委员会的成员，这是另一个批评该政权的国会机构。由于不同的原因，德克萨斯州看起来特别敏感。微信是一款消息传递和多功能应用程序，估计有 150 万美国用户，主要集中在华裔人口众多的州。华裔美国人约占德克萨斯州人口的百分之一。中国政府对微信的审查是有据可查的。
德克萨斯大学 2025 年的一项研究基于对德克萨斯州 20 名华裔美国人的采访，详细介绍了政治错误信息如何在该平台上传播。 一位年轻的受访者描述了她的父亲如何在实际选举前几个月读到一名亚裔美国女性当选波士顿市长。 “他只是接受他读到的所有内容，然后转发，”她说。 “我婆婆也是。”文化和社会压力降低了纠正家人或朋友群体中的错误信息的意愿。 “我感觉不对长辈说坏话，尤其是在群聊环境中，”一名 19 岁的华裔美国人解释道。在这种环境下，该应用程序的功能就很强大。 “很多人不知道该投票给谁，所以很容易受到影响，”另一位受访者评论道。 “这是一个很大的政治平台，很多人都会盲目跟随。”获取最新注册以定期接收带宽电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作情况。

No research shows Chinese propaganda or disinformation playing a pivotal role in the midterm elections, particularly when compared to Russia’s aggressive attempts. Yet significant blind spots exist. If it desired, Beijing is well-positioned to shape political debate through the WeChat app and through Chinese AI models. Rather than shifting control of Congress, Beijing’s goal would likely be to reduce the presence of known Communist Party critics, particularly those serving in the Congressional-Executive Commission on China. Created by Congress in October 2000, the Commission monitors Chinese human rights and rule of law. Several competitive races feature Commission members, including former Senator Sherrod Brown in Ohio and current Commission Chair Dan Sullivan in Alaska. House races in Iowa and Virginia involve current Commission members Zach Nunn and Jen Kiggans. Ashley Hinson, who is running for the Senate in Iowa, is on the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, another Congressional body critical of the regime. Texas looks particularly sensitive for a different reason. WeChat , a messaging and multi-function app, has an estimated 1.5 million US users, concentrated in states with large Chinese American populations. Chinese Americans  make up roughly one percent of  Texas’s population .  Chinese state-sponsored censorship  on WeChat is well-documented. A 2025 University of Texas study based on interviews with 20 Chinese Americans in Texas detailed how political misinformation circulates on the platform. One young interviewee described how her father read that an Asian American woman had been elected mayor of Boston months before the actual election. “He just accepts everything he reads, and then he just forwards it,” she said. “My mother-in-law, too.” Cultural and social pressures reduce willingness to correct misinformation in family or friend groups. “It doesn’t feel right for me to talk bad to my elders, especially in the group chat setting,” a 19-year-old Chinese American explained. In this environment, the app is powerful. “A lot of people don’t know who to vote for, so they are easily swayed,” another interviewee commented. “It is a big political platform, and a lot of people will just blindly follow.” Get the Latest Sign up to receive regular Bandwidth emails and stay informed about CEPA's work. The 2026 elections are the first to take place in an environment where AI chatbots are widely available. About one-fifth of Americans plan to use AI tools to help learn about candidates or inform voting decisions, according to a recent survey . Most will turn to American models such as ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Perplexity, but many US developers are increasingly relying on Chinese-origin models such as DeepSeek and Qwen, allowing them to enter the US information environment. These models reflect the Chinese government’s official stances on domestic politics and human rights. Censorship and propaganda have also been found  in responses to questions about US press freedom and elections. One study examined Chinese AI models’ responses to questions about the upcoming US elections. Conducted by a research group based in Europe, researchers tested seven AI models (five US and two Chinese) with a set of 20 polling-style questions. All models proved relatively consistent and offered mixed results in terms of partisan preferences. The two Chinese models did not diverge sharply from their US counterparts in their responses. DeepSeek, for example, selected the Democratic option on two questions about which party’s candidate it would select for Congress and which party it prefers to control Congress. So did Claude and Perplexity (99% on one of the questions). By contrast, Qwen chose Democrats 55% and 75% of the time, respectively. The results are striking for what they show about the leeway allowed the Chinese models to comment on US versus Chinese politics. DeepSeek offered critical assessments of the US president’s job performance. Asking the same questions about Chinese President Xi Jinping would almost certainly produce refusals or strictly glowing reviews. Major holes remain in our understanding of where and how Chinese Communist Party-linked electoral influence could be occurring. Researchers, election monitors, and others focused on election integrity should address these gaps — particularly before the 2028 elections. Sarah Cook is founder of China Rights Analytics and Advising LLC and author of the UnderReported China newsletter. title: India Stall Opens in Central Asia’s Military Bazaar
zh_title: 印度摊位在中亚军事集市上开业
source: 欧洲政策分析中心 （CEPA） - CEPA
summary: 虽然人们的注意力主要集中在中国侵入中亚经济和安全领域，从而削弱俄罗斯的实力，但随着该地区军事采购多元化，印度已成为新的武器销售国。 10月初，印度国防部长拉杰什·库马尔·辛格证实，印度已向塔吉克斯坦出口其国产的阿卡什防空系统。该系统可以在最远约 25 公里（16 英里）的范围内拦截飞机、直升机和无人机。新德里还确认向土库曼斯坦出口同一系统，此前土库曼斯坦一直依赖该系统
content:
虽然人们的注意力主要集中在中国侵入中亚经济和安全领域，从而削弱俄罗斯的实力，但随着该地区军事采购多元化，印度已成为新的武器销售国。 10月初，印度国防部长拉杰什·库马尔·辛格证实，印度已向塔吉克斯坦出口其国产的阿卡什防空系统。该系统可以在最远约 25 公里（16 英里）的范围内拦截飞机、直升机和无人机。新德里还确认向土库曼斯坦出口同一系统，该国此前一直依赖俄罗斯和中国的防空设备。其他安全领域的合作也不断扩大。 9月至10月，印度和哈萨克斯坦举行了Kazind-2026联合军演，两国约有60名军事人员参加。此前，印度-乌兹别克斯坦于 4 月举行了“Dustlik-2026”演习，并与吉尔吉斯斯坦举行了类似的演习。印度还加强了与乌兹别克斯坦、吉尔吉斯斯坦和塔吉克斯坦的安全协调和反恐努力、军事技术磋商和情报合作。 2025年6月在新德里举行的印度-中亚外长安全对话重申了打击恐怖主义、恐怖主义融资、武器贩运和毒品贩运的合作。印度的进展很重要。
这标志着中亚的军事采购总体上摆脱了对俄罗斯的严重依赖，俄罗斯喜欢将该地区视为自己的后院。印度并不是中亚国家唯一求助的参与者。例如，中国在过去几年中通过向乌兹别克斯坦出售成都歼10CE喷气式飞机来扩大其在该地区的地位，乌兹别克斯坦是继巴基斯坦之后第二个接收飞机的国家。据报道，哈萨克斯坦也有兴趣从中国购买六架K-8W轻型战斗机。还有土耳其，其紧凑型无人机在纳戈尔诺-卡拉巴赫战争以及乌克兰和伊朗持续冲突中的表现对中亚国家越来越有吸引力。尽管印度对中亚的武器销售仍然相对较少，但中国武器在该地区的存在不断增加，表明该地区的力量平衡可能发生重大的长期变化。自20世纪90年代以来，俄罗斯一直是中亚国家的主要军事和安全伙伴，这一地位体现在其广泛的军事基地网络、双边防务协议和多边安全安排上。获取最新注册以接收定期电子邮件并随时了解 CEPA 的工作。

While attention mostly falls upon China’s inroads into Central Asia’s economic and security spheres, so undercutting Russia, India has emerged as a new seller of weapons as the region diversifies its military procurement. In early October, Indian Defense Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh confirmed that India had exported its domestically developed Akash air-defense system to Tajikistan. The system can intercept aircraft, helicopters, and drones at ranges of up to approximately 25 km (16 miles). New Delhi also confirmed the export of the same system to Turkmenistan, which had previously been reliant on Russian- and Chinese-origin air-defense equipment. Cooperation has also expanded in other security fields. In September-October, India and Kazakhstan held the Kazind-2026 joint military exercise involving approximately 60 military personnel from each country. This followed the India-Uzbekistan exercises, Dustlik-2026, held in April and a similar drill held with Kyrgyzstan. India has likewise stepped up security coordination and counterterrorism efforts, military-technical consultations, and intelligence-related cooperation with Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan. The India-Central Asia foreign ministers’ security dialogue held in June 2025 in New Delhi reaffirmed cooperation against terrorism, terrorist financing, arms trafficking, and narcotics trafficking. India’s inroads matter. It signals a general shift in Central Asia’s military procurement away from a heavy dependence on Russia, which likes to regard the region as its backyard. India is not the only actor Central Asian countries are turning to. China, for example, has in the past few years expanded its position in the region by selling Chengdu J-10CE jets to Uzbekistan, the second country to take delivery after Pakistan. Kazakhstan is also reportedly interested in purchasing six K-8W light-combat aircraft from China. There is also Turkey with its compact drones that have become increasingly attractive for Central Asian countries following their performance in the wars for Nagorno-Karabakh, and amid the ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. Although Indian arms sales to Central Asia remain relatively modest, the growing presence of Chinese weaponry in the region points to a potentially significant long-term shift in the regional balance of power. Since the 1990s, Russia has served as the predominant military and security partner for Central Asian states, a position reflected in its extensive network of military bases, bilateral defense agreements, and multilateral security arrangements. Russian domination of Central Asia’s military procurement began to change in the early 2020s, particularly following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The prolonged conflict has placed considerable strain on Russia’s military-industrial capacity, limiting Moscow’s ability to meet the defense requirements of its traditional partners. Russia has consequently faced growing difficulties in fulfilling arms orders and supplying military equipment to allies and partners, including Belarus, Armenia, and several Central Asian states. These constraints have prompted Central Asian governments to diversify military procurement, creating new opportunities for India to expand its defense exports and strengthen security cooperation across the five republics. Although Russia remains an important military partner, India’s growing role and that of China could gradually erode Moscow’s position. More importantly, the implications of this trend extend beyond the immediate sale of military equipment. The acquisition of Indian weapons systems creates longer-term technological and logistical ties, as recipient countries will require Indian expertise, spare parts, maintenance services, technical training, and modernization support. Over time, these dependencies could translate into deeper institutional ties between Indian defense industries and Central Asian armed forces. Seen from a wider perspective, India’s military outreach to Central Asia is part of New Delhi’s search for more active relations with the region. The engagement increasingly consists of developing regional trade routes (especially on the north-south axis), bilateral commerce, investments into critical infrastructure and cooperation on potential security spillover from Afghanistan, all of them exemplified in the visits made by Indian prime minister Narendra Modi to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan earlier this year. New Delhi and Tashkent elevated their relationship to a comprehensive strategic partnership and agreed to work on connectivity, education and, most of all, critical minerals. Indian weaponry, coupled with that of other non-traditional suppliers, creates a qualitatively different balance of power in Central Asia. What currently appears to be a relatively limited expansion of Indian arms exports could eventually become an important driver of a broader redistribution of military and security influence in Central Asia, gradually challenging Moscow’s and, to a certain extent, Beijing’s influence in the region. content: 陈延年 国际社会主义道路（ISA） 当前，台湾同志权利面临日益严峻攻击。极右翼组织台联党于去年12月2日发表政策顾问社论，利用民众对中共的恐惧，散播「中国来台男同婚占九成」的假消息，将跨国同婚抹黑为让「中共渗透」的「国安危机」。 尽管民进党政府在随后澄清，自2024年开放两岸同婚以来，仅有130对伴侣结婚，且女同志更多。民进党对于台联党攻击同志平权的抹黑攻击，民进党极其驯服，仅止于数据交代，从未严厉谴责，深怕得罪与台联党持同样立场的亲绿右翼支持者。这再次暴露了民进党为巩固政权，不惜牺牲性别平权与民主权利的本质（参见第77期《社会主义者》「争取性别平等的斗争：为什么民进党并非站在我们这边」）。 蓝白恐同本色 为避免流失右翼选票，民进党政府急忙强调将以「国安」为由，强化对跨国伴侣的审查。然而，我们没理由相信，从未真正保护劳工免于过劳死与职灾威胁的亲资政党们，如民进党和台联。他们口中的「国安」从非保护人民安全，而是为了掩护其打压同志及剥夺群众民主权利的行径。 此外，民进党政府去年12月预告修改《体位区分标准》，原版草案本来要强迫间性人与「未经性别重置手术」的跨性别女性服兵役，民进党一度采纳了极右势力的说法，以巩固权力，他们将跨性别女性认同抹黑为「逃兵手段」。后来，由于进步群体的反弹民进党才打消。 然而多数跨性别者根本没有机会在服役年龄前获得「诊断书」，以让她们得以免除兵役。 台联党早在去年10月的声明中就利用民众对中共的恐惧，并散播亲军国主义的意识形态，诬陷过跨女认同是逃避兵役的手段，这种做法故意无视了军队体制中严重的父权色彩与性骚扰频传的事实，更遑论强迫剪发等否定性别认同的体制压力，这必将造成长期的心理创伤。——由大商家权贵把持的政府，为了用军国主义转移焦点，让群众为这个剥削且压迫的制度继续流血，极度仰赖右翼民族主义者，因为他们用国安包裹压迫。 面对绿营势力对同志的攻击，国民党与民众党选择沉默，因为若公开反对，将疏离其保守的恐同支持者；若公开支持，则会无法与民进党区隔、暴露亲军国主义真面目，进而疏离那些因反对民进党滥用战争威胁才「别无选择」靠向蓝营的群体。 蓝白恐同劣迹斑斑。国民党曾扬言若完全执政将取消同婚；党主席郑丽文也早已放弃公开支持同婚。民众党主席柯文哲则曾在公投中对同婚投下反对票，并提拔「反同大将」李国宪担任要职。蓝白为了与民进党竞逐，把国安的概念换成和平修辞和与中共谈判的幻想。 社群媒体Dcard上一名使用者揭露，成功岭替代役新训期间，只是因为发现性行为，高层就展开了全连强迫出柜的性倾向调查，而执行该调查的正是军事独裁保留至今的宪兵，以恐同肃整军队就是他们眼中的「秩序」，反观若有异性恋性行为根本不会展开「你是异性恋吗？」如此全面调查。 反对迎合军国主义 沃草与妇女新知等民团主张将「多元视角纳入民防」视为国安战略，这种论述极其危险，因为当前的「国安」与「民防」概念，在现实中是强化资本统治与军国主义的工具，所谓的「多元参与」势必沦为动员弱势群体为军国主义服务的工具，这将进一步加深对女性、身障者及劳工的现有压迫。 当前统治阶级以「全民防卫」之名，将战争准备正常化，动员LGBT+、女性与劳动群众作为炮灰。平权修辞无法掩盖军国主义本质，任何包装成「友善」的征兵或全民防卫都是对群众的欺骗。 若要发挥实质成效，抵抗恐同与性别压迫，必须与反军国主义结合。劳动阶级必须独立于蓝绿白及所有亲资亲帝势力，建立自己的政治力量与群众组织，在产业与社区中对抗战争威胁与既有压迫，拒绝为任何帝国主义竞逐牺牲。 正如中东是全球前列的军事开支地区，但显然军备竞赛无法带来安全，战争源于资本主义对利润与地缘权力的争夺。唯有建设战斗性的工运与工人政党，将军费与国安预算转向公共住房、教育与医疗，并与各国劳动者团结抵抗战争机器，才能真正反对压迫，终结资本主义制造的战争。■   這篇文章 以「国安」为名的恐同攻击 最早出現於 中国劳工论坛 China Worker 。

title: 美日韩外长在G20外长会议间隙举行三方会谈，再度确认台海和平稳定重要性

content: 资料照片：美国国务卿马尔科·卢比奥在纽约联合国大会期间会见日本外相茂木敏充(Motegi Toshimitsu)(右)和韩国外交部长赵显(Cho Hyun)(左)，三国外长在会后发表联合声明。(2026年9月21日) 华盛顿 — 美国、日本与韩国外长上星期五(10月30日)在亚特兰大举行的20国集团(G20)外长会议期间举行三方会谈。美国国务院说，三方外长在会中再次强调了维持台海和平稳定的重要性；美国国务卿马科尔·卢比奥(Marco Rubio)也在会中提到，中国在南中国海、东中国海及黄海的胁迫行为，以及与俄罗斯的合作都是在破坏印太地区的和平稳定。 旨在为下个月在美国佛罗里达州迈阿密举行的20国集团领导人峰会铺垫的外长会议，讨论议程包括航行自由、能源、粮食及供应链安全的议题。 美国国务院在当天发布的声明中说，卢比奥与日本外相茂木敏充(Motegi Toshimitsu)及韩国外长赵显(Cho Hyun)在会议间隙进行了三方会谈，“审视了促进自由开放印太地区安全与繁荣的三边伙伴关系”，并签署了一个“三边北极太平洋伙伴关系(TAPP)”合作备忘录，以探索在太平洋北极地区的海洋合作与经济伙伴关系。 声明指出，国务卿与两位外长重申他们致力于实现朝鲜民主主义人民共和国的完全无核化，并全面执行联合国安理会各项决议，包括禁止为朝鲜核计划及弹道导弹项目提供创收支持。 “他们也强调了维护台海和平稳定的重要性。卢比奥国务卿也提出了中国寻求在南中国海确立控制权的举措、其在东中国海及黄海的胁迫行为，以及俄罗斯与中国损害印太地区和平稳定的合作，”声明说。 三国外长前一次会谈是在9月21日联合国大会期间，当时三方会谈后也曾发布联合声明，强调维系台海和平稳定的重要性。 国务院说，此次三人再度确认了该次会面时发布的共同声明，并承诺将继续在所有级别开展三方会谈。 台湾外交部上星期六发布声明表示，外长林佳龙对三国外长再次确认台海和平稳定重要性表达感谢，并欢迎伙伴国家持续透过具体行动维护区域整体和平稳定。 “美日韩三国外长今年已多次公开重申维护台海和平稳定的重要性，充分彰显台海安全攸关区域稳定，已是国际社会高度关切的共同议题，更是维系印太区域和平与繁荣不可或缺的一环，”声明说。 台湾外交部强调，面对中国持续升高对台军事威胁及灰色地带侵扰，台湾将持续与美国及其他理念相近国家深化合作，共同维护台海及印太地区的和平、稳定与繁荣。

title: 仅发电邮邀请出席APEC峰会，台湾抗议中国“歧视性待遇”
summary: 资料照片：台湾外交部长林佳龙在台北举行的新闻发布会上讲话。(2024年7月19日) 台湾外交部长林佳龙星期一(11月2日)表示，即将在深圳举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会，主办方中国仅以电子邮件而不是正式信函邀请台湾，台湾已经向中国发出正式抗议；但台湾不会因为遭到歧视性待遇，就放弃参与的权利。 中国将在这个月18日-19日于广东深圳主办2026年APEC第33次领导人非正式会议，包括美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladim
content: 资料照片：台湾外交部长林佳龙在台北举行的新闻发布会上讲话。(2024年7月19日) 台湾外交部长林佳龙星期一(11月2日)表示，即将在深圳举行的亚太经合组织(APEC)峰会，主办方中国仅以电子邮件而不是正式信函邀请台湾，台湾已经向中国发出正式抗议；但台湾不会因为遭到歧视性待遇，就放弃参与的权利。 中国将在这个月18日-19日于广东深圳主办2026年APEC第33次领导人非正式会议，包括美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladimir Putin)以及全球商界领袖和国际组织负责人都将出席。 台湾外交部长林佳龙星期一表示，今年中国并未循例亲自递交邀请函，而是以电子邮件寄送，林佳龙表示，台湾已经在第一时间向中国表达抗议。 依照惯例，APEC主办国会派特使亲自递送邀请函。林佳龙表示，今年中方没有采取亲自递交的方式，而是以“电子邮件”联系台湾外交部，称谓则维持台湾的参与名称“Chinese Taipei”(中华台北)。 台湾中央社报道，林佳龙星期一在接受记者访问时表示，台湾作为APEC正式会员，过去平等参与领导人峰会，中国在争取这次主办时也承诺，会遵守APEC规章、惯例，并确保出席国家代表有平等地位和安全。 林佳龙指出，今年各种APEC相关会议，中国对台湾有一些差别待遇，台湾外交部都立即表达抗议，并争取台湾的参与权益，也与APEC所有会员经济体保持良好沟通，获得支持。 林佳龙强调，台湾不会因为中国企图施加差别待遇，就放弃参与APEC的权益，也希望中国就邀请函递送、称谓和程序，都能遵守相关规定。 台湾在1991年11月以“ Chinese Taipei”名义，与中国大陆、香港一同加入APEC，是APEC正式成员。 APEC领导人峰会从1993年开始，由于北京反对台湾总统出席，台湾通常由总统指派一名“领袖代表”参加。长期以来，APEC峰会主办国派特使到台北，向台湾总统递交邀请函，台湾总统再指派代表出席。不过具体做法随主办国不同和两岸关系发展而有变化。 2001年中国在上海主办APEC峰会，北京向台北发出传真通知，而不是派特使递交正式邀请，随后北京拒绝了时任台湾总统陈水扁选定的代表，卸任副总统李元簇，台湾因此没有派代表出席当年的领导人峰会。 2014年中国再次主办峰会，时任台湾总统为马英九。中国派出国台办副主任龚清概到台北，向时任台湾陆委会主委王郁琦递交邀请。 今年，台湾外交部长林佳龙证实已经收到中方邀请，但邀请函是以“电子邮件”发出，台湾已经向主办方提出抗议。但表示不会因此放弃参与。 过去几个月，两岸关系因中国的灰色地带侵扰持续紧张。中国加大在台湾附近海域的军事与海警活动，台湾方面10月底也报告侦测到多批中国军机和舰船。 台湾中央社报道，台湾陆委会副主委沈有忠星期一在台北出席亚洲政经与和平交流协会举行的一场研讨会上表示，预计中国在五中全会后，可能加大对台湾的灰色地带施压，频繁使用海警船、科研船、民兵船等非正规军事力量，在不引发全面军事冲突的前提下，挑战台日菲等区域民主国家在这片海域的管辖权和执法权，企图逐步改变国际航行自由的现状。 上个月20日，中国海警船进入东沙海域限制水域，台湾派出海巡舰艇监控并进行驱离。 美国国务院对此向美国之音表示，中国的行为是蓄意的胁迫和破坏稳定的(intentionally coercive and destabilizing)。国务院发言人指出，中国在台湾和平管辖了70多年的海域周边宣示权威，只会加剧紧张局势，破坏地区和平与安全。

title: ACM Research Announces Shipment of Its First 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p Panel-Level Horizontal Electroplating Production Tool
zh_title: ACM Research 宣布发货其首款 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产工具
summary: 半导体和先进封装应用晶圆加工解决方案供应商 ACM Research, Inc. 今天宣布向中国大陆以外的亚洲客户发货其首个 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产系统。此次发货标志着 ACM 核心面板级技术的又一重大进步，也是在拓宽其多产品平台和扩大全球客户影响力方面向前迈出的重要一步。随着先进封装技术的不断发展，面板级加工越来越受到关注
content:
半导体和先进封装应用晶圆加工解决方案供应商 ACM Research, Inc. 今天宣布向中国大陆以外的亚洲客户发货其首个 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产系统。此次发货标志着 ACM 核心面板级技术的又一重大进步，也是在拓宽其多产品平台和扩大全球客户影响力方面向前迈出的重要一步。随着先进封装技术的不断发展，面板级处理因其适应更大基板的能力而在整个行业中受到关注。电镀是先进封装制造中最关键的步骤之一，其中设备稳定性、镀层厚度均匀性和一致性对于成功的工艺集成、产品良率和制造效率至关重要。新发货的工具专为 310 × 310 mm 面板级应用而设计，展示了 ACM 根据客户要求快速推进产品开发的能力。在此之前，ACM 首款 515 × 510 mm 研发工具于去年发货，突显了 ACM 将技术突破快速商业化至规模生产的能力。 “这是 ACM 先进封装工作的一个重要里程碑，标志着我们向亚洲客户交付了世界上第一个 310 × 310 毫米面板级水平电镀生产工具，”ACM 博士说。
ACM Research 总裁兼首席执行官 David Wang 表示：“我们相信，我们专有的水平电镀技术具有独特的优势，能够实现跨多种面板尺寸和新兴封装架构的下一代先进半导体封装。随着人工智能推动日益复杂的封装要求，我们看到了 ACM 在这个快速发展的市场中发挥推动作用的重要长期机会。” Ultra ECP ap-p 系统采用 ACM 专有的水平电镀技术，支持铜 (Cu)、镍 (Ni)、锡银 (SnAg) 和金 (Au) 电镀工艺。其铜电镀室采用专为高铜柱应用设计的高速电镀桨，能够在高电镀速率下为 300 微米铜柱实现良好的芯片内均匀性。该系统还具有四面密封干接触吸盘，可提高可靠性；单元内冲洗功能可最大限度地减少不同电镀单元之间的化学交叉污染；水平电镀设计采用 ACM 正在申请专利的技术，使吸盘的旋转与旋转矩形电场同步，从而实现卓越的沉积均匀性。除了设备交付之外，ACM 还致力于通过提供高质量设备、支持可靠的批量生产和提供可靠的技术支持来建立长期的客户关系。
ACM将继续推进技术进步，拓展多产品平台，扩大全球客户群。ACM旨在通过与全球合作伙伴的合作，支持人工智能行业的发展，并以其差异化的半导体设备技术为客户创造更大的价值。 ACM Research 宣布其首款 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p 面板级水平电镀生产工具发货的消息首先出现在《半导体文摘》上。

【原文 English Original】
ACM Research, Inc. , a supplier of wafer processing solutions for semiconductor and advanced packaging applications, today announced the shipment of its first 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p panel-level horizontal electroplating production system to a customer in Asia outside mainland China. The shipment marks another significant advance in ACM’s core panel-level technologies and represents an important step forward in broadening its multi-product platform and expanding its global customer presence. As advanced packaging technologies continue to evolve, panel-level processing is gaining traction across the industry for its ability to accommodate larger substrates. Electroplating is one of the most critical steps in advanced packaging manufacturing, where equipment stability, plating thickness uniformity and consistency are essential to successful process integration, product yield and manufacturing efficiency. The newly shipped tool is designed for 310 × 310 mm panel-level applications, and demonstrates ACM’s ability to quickly advance product development per customer requirements. This follows last year’s shipment of ACM’s first 515 × 510 mm R&D tool, highlighting ACM’s ability to rapidly commercialize technical breakthroughs into scale production. “This is an important milestone for ACM’s advanced packaging efforts, and marks shipment of what we believe is the world’s first 310 × 310 mm panel-level horizontal electroplating production tool to a customer in Asia,” said Dr. David Wang, President and Chief Executive Officer of ACM Research. “We believe our proprietary horizontal plating technology is uniquely positioned to enable the next generation of advanced semiconductor packaging across multiple panel sizes and emerging packaging architectures. As AI drives increasingly complex packaging requirements, we see a significant long-term opportunity for ACM to play an enabling role in this rapidly evolving market.” The Ultra ECP ap-p system features ACM’s proprietary horizontal electroplating technology and supports copper (Cu), nickel (Ni), tin-silver (SnAg) and gold (Au) plating processes. Its copper plating chamber incorporates a high-speed plating paddle specifically designed for tall copper pillar applications, capable of achieving good within-die uniformity for 300-micron copper pillars at high plating rates. The system also features a four-sided sealing dry contact chuck for improved reliability, in-cell rinse functionality to minimize chemical cross-contamination between different plating cells, and a horizontal electroplating design that uses ACM’s patent-pending technology to synchronize the rotation of the chuck with a rotating rectangular electric field for superior deposition uniformity. Beyond equipment delivery, ACM is committed to building long-term customer relationships by providing high-quality equipment, supporting reliable volume production and delivering reliable technical support. ACM will continue to advance its technologies, expand its multi-product platform and grow its global customer base. Through collaboration with partners worldwide, ACM aims to support the growth of the AI industry and create greater value for customers with its differentiated semiconductor equipment technologies. The post ACM Research Announces Shipment of Its First 310 × 310 mm Ultra ECP ap-p Panel-Level Horizontal Electroplating Production Tool appeared first on Semiconductor Digest .

title: 法國示威・巴黎直擊｜示威者為何上街？居法香港學者拆解香港、法國抗爭之別
summary: 追光者 2026-11-5 【 法國示威・巴黎直擊｜示威者為何上街？居法香港學者拆解香港、法國抗爭之別 】 席捲整個法國的示威浪潮持續，全國周四（6日）有多達200場示威。今波抗爭始於高中生不滿政府對教育撥款不足，不過到工會「接力」時卻加入調高最低工資等訴求，這是一場「騎劫」嗎？香港主流傳媒亦藉法國今場抗爭與7年前的「反送中運動」相提並論，兩者又有可比性嗎？ 法國高中學生面對教師不足、校舍老鼠為患，甚至連桌椅都欠缺的學習環境，於是近月憤而以堵塞校園、上街示威等手段表達不滿。
content: 追光者  2026-11-5 【 法國示威・巴黎直擊｜示威者為何上街？居法香港學者拆解香港、法國抗爭之別 】 席捲整個法國的示威浪潮持續，全國周四（6日）有多達200場示威。今波抗爭始於高中生不滿政府對教育撥款不足，不過到工會「接力」時卻加入調高最低工資等訴求，這是一場「騎劫」嗎？香港主流傳媒亦藉法國今場抗爭與7年前的「反送中運動」相提並論，兩者又有可比性嗎？ 法國高中學生面對教師不足、校舍老鼠為患，甚至連桌椅都欠缺的學習環境，於是近月憤而以堵塞校園、上街示威等手段表達不滿。不過工會周四發起的大罷工，雖然一方面聲稱是要聲援學生抗爭，但另一方面同時加入了爭取提高最低工資、要求政府修訂財政預算等訴求。 法國全國總工會（CGT）亞洲及大洋洲地區經濟政策顧問 Sylvain Goldstein 周四遊行前接受《追光者》訪問，被問到工會加入會否令學生訴求失焦時，強調兩個群體的訴求背後是源於同一個問題，「如果你（打工仔）有好的薪酬，他們就可以負擔社會保障費（social contribution），可以買椅子、書桌、為教師支薪；但如果人工低，就不能買不同的東西」。 那高中生會認為自己的貢獻被「騎劫」嗎？與朋友參與示威的 Rose 交代自己為何參與遊行時，卻表示自己是為展示與法國勞動階層的團結所以走上街頭：「因為我們其實正陷於經濟危機，即是政府不能滿足我們的期望，像我們1968年5月還是很富有那時。所以我認為，如果我們不起革命推翻這個政府，是不會有任何改變的」。 示威群眾裏有一張亞洲面孔與不同示威者交流，原來他是居於法國的香港政治哲學學者 Kenneth，自2015年就開始研究法國不同面向的抗爭，除了曾跟隨「黃背心」示威，實地作資料搜集外，亦會在不同光譜的抗爭者聚會中進行觀察。 他指法國抗爭文化向來容納不同訴求、不同聲音，但遇到有人「搶光環」時，有時出於政治現實等考量未必會選擇直接表達，「（例如）唔係話『個政黨唔代表我』就可以了結到嘅一件事，要考慮形勢等各樣嘢，未必會選擇喺公開或者媒體嘅場合咁樣出聲，然後可能喺其他嘅地方繼續做佢哋自己抗爭嘅工作，我覺得呢個位係比較 subtle（微妙）」。 另一邊廂，香港「黨媒」眼見法國示威上月底出現搶掠等情況仿似「如獲至寶」，試圖以此「唱好」香港《國安法》所帶來的「穩定」。不過 Kenneth 認為兩地示威文化不同，根本難以作類比，「其實早幾年法國都有過國安法嘅問題… 其實佢哋都有出來示威，呢啲法例哪怕係喺一個民主制度嘅社會，佢哋會擔心呢個民主制度會點樣崩塌嘅時候，其實都好多人出來示威」。 Kenneth 又提到，上街遊行甚至與警察爆發衝突，只屬於法國抗爭文化的一部分，沒有示威的日子他們亦會在書店等地方有不同的活動、聚會，一直經營著不同的抗爭群體，形容「香港抗爭文化嘅累積比法國人少」，但到2019年曾經曇花一現的同類文化實在「消失得太快」。

title: 李承鹏：习近平能不能永久连任
summary: 李承鹏（大眼哥） X @dayangelcp · Nov 5, 2026 我的油管第14期：《习近平能不能永久连任》 电影《黑社会》之龙城风云里，邓肥说：“黑社会也是有权力制约的，不能一人独大，要平衡。几十年的规矩改了，社团的叔父们一定会很不舒服。” 可中南海的叔父们，要么找马克思和毛主席报到去了，要么住进了秦城的豪华一居室，剩下的只能在特勤局监视下种种花、养养鸟、听听戏…… 如果在一家公司，他必须是董事长、总裁、CEO一肩挑；在帮派，他必须是帮主、执法长老、执棒长老一肩挑。
content: 李承鹏（大眼哥） X @dayangelcp  · Nov 5, 2026 我的油管第14期：《习近平能不能永久连任》 电影《黑社会》之龙城风云里，邓肥说：“黑社会也是有权力制约的，不能一人独大，要平衡。几十年的规矩改了，社团的叔父们一定会很不舒服。” 可中南海的叔父们，要么找马克思和毛主席报到去了，要么住进了秦城的豪华一居室，剩下的只能在特勤局监视下种种花、养养鸟、听听戏…… 如果在一家公司，他必须是董事长、总裁、CEO一肩挑；在帮派，他必须是帮主、执法长老、执棒长老一肩挑。未来权力排序不是一号人物、二号人物、三号人物……而是一号人物之下，全是打工仔。中南海权力体系不再是金字塔形状，而是倒T字形。 习近平会永久连任吗？ 党指挥枪VS枪杆子里面出政权，其实是孪生兄弟。谁当党老大，必须是枪老大，否则必然被拿下；谁是枪老大，就是党老大，你有枪别人就听话。 没有蓝玉没有年羹尧没有袁世凯，整个军队像玩乐高一样拆了拼、拼了拆。谁手里都凑不齐一支完整部队，没有中间管理层，瓜子二手车，没有中间商赚差价。 会上演《南山的部长们》吗？会有玄武门之变吗？张又侠老部下会拎着两把板斧劫法场吗？谁是“铁帽子王”？ 世界上有个独裁者困境：如果指定接班人，接班人很快成为权力副中心，独裁者权力就被稀释；如果不指定接班人，死后又要被清算。 谜一般，习主席到底有没有指定接班人——指定早了，就成了刘少奇，晚了，就成了华国锋，能力强，就是林彪，能力差，就是王洪文。毛泽东临死前一年才让华国锋当副总理兼公安部长。汉武帝临死前，才立刘弗陵为太子。康熙临终病榻前，才传位给雍正，传位诏书放在“正大光明”牌匾后面，一点都不正大光明。 《威权统治的政治学》统计：从1946到2008年，303个非正常下台的独裁者，被民众起义推翻的只有32个，10个里面不到一个。而这303个非正常下台的独裁者里，205个是被统治集团内部的人赶下台的，占三分之二以上。独裁者真正防的不是街上的民众，而是会议室里的小弟。 最刺激的是突尼斯的布尔吉巴，他独裁三十一年，精心挑选最信任的本·阿里当接班人。可一个多月后的某天夜里，本·阿里把七个医生召到内政部，让他们签字证明——老领导精神失常了。 有医生不干，本·阿里一拍桌子“老子数到三”……医生马上服软。自从得了精神病，我的精神好多了。第二天老领导被软禁在一处大宅子里，一直到死去。 未来漫长岁月，总有天意，所谓天意，就是每个人的心意。 习近平到底能不能永久连任，点击进入： 李承鹏（大眼哥） @dayangelcp · 2h 习近平会不会永久连任？看看王莽，俩人活像孪生兄弟。年轻时都谦虚低调，恭敬节俭。俩人都心怀不忍，接济黎民百姓。俩人都具有史命感，王莽想回到“周公盛世”，习近平要“中华民族伟大复兴”。俩人都玩国进民退，百业凋敝。 王莽因为猜忌，至死没解决接班人问题。习主席已七十三岁，接班人也习惯性流产。 独裁者困境：如果指定接班人，官员们会向未来皇帝靠拢，接班人成为权力副中心，独裁者权力就被稀释；但如果不指定接班人，死后又被清算——斯大林没指定接班人，赫鲁晓夫上位后全盘否定斯大林，遗体都迁出了列宁墓。 习主席不能公开指定接班人，形成权力副中心。又必须选定可靠接班人，以免死后被翻盘。独裁者永远找不到安全交权方式。民主选举吵吵闹闹，但有基本制度保障。独裁者交班，步步惊心，杀机四伏，老命都得搭进去。 习主席当然会指定接班人，但指定早了，就成了刘少奇；晚了，成了华国锋；能力强，成了林彪；能力差，就成了王洪文。《威权统治的政治学》统计：1946到2008年303个非正常下台的独裁者，被民众起义推翻的只有32个，不到十分之一。303个非正常下台的独裁者里，205个是被统治集团内部的人赶下去的，占三分之二以上。 独裁者真正要防的，不是街上的民众，而是会议室里的小弟。 著名的例子是安哥拉独裁者多斯桑托斯，执政三十八年。2016年精心指定了接班人。没想到接班人和军队结盟。一上任就清算。逼的多斯桑托斯流亡，客死他乡。 哈萨克斯坦的纳扎尔巴耶夫，独裁三十年，2019年传位给最信任的接班人，接班人把首都改名“努尔苏丹”——纳扎尔巴耶夫的尊号。此举向老领导表忠心、向世人秀恩爱。可是秀恩爱，死得快。一年后，这名接班人就清算纳扎尔巴耶夫，还逼他公开承认自己“不过是个退休人员”。这叫杀人诛心。 摆在独裁者面前的世纪难题，你永远不知道，眼前这些忠心耿耿的接班人，李强？蔡奇？丁薛祥？哪个会突然跳出来捅你刀子。 更刺激的是突尼斯的布尔吉巴，独裁三十一年，挑选最信任的本·阿里当接班人，可一个多月后的某天夜里，本·阿里把七个医生召到内政部，让他们签字，证明老领导精神失常了。有医生不干，本.阿里一拍桌子，老子数到三…… 第二天老领导就下台了，被软禁在一处大宅子里，一直到死去。 自从得了精神病，我的精神好多了。习近平会不会永久连任？关注我的油管号： https:// youtube.com/channel/UCye2h ———————————————— wJV7IRisIcGSUpQbVw?si=UWEkRJrIAX9_mqjl 李承鹏（大眼哥） @dayangelcp · 4h 习近平会不会永久连任，先看看他与哪位历史人物最像。他跟王莽活像孪生兄弟。  俩人年轻时都朴实谦虚。《汉书》说王莽“折节为恭俭”，能放下外戚子弟的身段，待人恭敬、节俭。王家子弟个个穿戴奢华，只有王莽穿布衣，活像穷书生。   习近平作为副国级高干子弟，十五岁到梁家河插队，住窑洞，吃粗粮，穿粗衣，身上长跳蚤，扛着锄头下地干活。跟那些北京来的知青完全不一样。   王莽乐善好施，车马皮衣都分给门客。习近平碰上个从米脂一路讨饭过来的老汉，心中不忍，把身上的钱和粮票掏光，连外套都脱下来给了老汉。   王莽替穷人办事，在长安城盖了两百所住宅，安置贫民。习近平在宁德时眼见一万三千多户船民挤在船上住，有人住在山上茅草屋。他立马在福安开现场会，让几万人搬进了新房。   为了让农民富起来，他自费学建沼气池。捅导管时，沼气喷涌而出，溅了满脸粪水。   王莽当上大司马，妻子穿着短衣布裙待客，客人还以为她是佣人。电视台来采访，彭丽媛抱着孩子，洗菜，炒菜，拖地，开饭时亲自端菜，要不是那张人人认识的脸，就是一个普通主妇。   每逢灾年，王莽只吃素，太后只得下诏，让他按时吃肉，爱惜身体。习近平冒着零下十几度严寒去看望灾区群众。晚饭只上了阜平炖菜、拍蒜茼蒿几个家常菜……   王莽上书捐钱百万、献田三十顷救济灾民，官员跟捐。疫情爆发，习近平带头捐款，全国党员官员共跟捐了116.3亿元。   俩人上位史也惊人相似。大司马王根病退前，目睹王莽种种仁义，推举他接替自己的职务。2007年曾庆红退休，深觉习近平低调憨厚，向老江推荐了习近平。王莽和习主席都以谦虚低调仁义才登得大位，都是人们发现时已无法挽回。王莽篡位后索要传国玉玺，王政君大骂王莽猪狗不如。江泽民、曾庆红后来目睹自己的人马被习一个个拿下，当年以裸退支持习上位的胡锦涛被公开架走，打碎了牙往肚里吞，权当是补钙了。   王莽为了消除贫富差距，打击土地兼并，天下田地收归国有，是为“王田”。习近平提出共同富裕，消除贫富差距，国进民退，是为“中国梦”。   王莽盐铁收归官府，滥改币制，开设官市，百姓苦不堪言。习近平肃整市场，国家队进场，百业凋敝，失业居高不下。王莽反贪，习近平反腐一直在路上。   王莽要回到周公盛世，习近平要中华民族伟大复兴。人们总说王莽是从未来穿越回汉朝的社会主义者，可谁说习总不是从两千年穿越到现在的王莽。   敬请加关注： https:// youtube.com/channel/UCye2h wJV7IRisIcGSUpQbVw?si=NIME9UtuSKr8XLgt _________________________________________ 李承鹏（大眼哥） @dayangelcp · 5h 深改组组长，网信组组长，军改组组长，财经组长，外事组长，对台组长，足球都没放过，以前中国足球恐韩恐伊，现在连越南都踢不过。过去中国足球“问君能有几多愁，恰似一群太监上青楼”，为啥？九十分钟不射啊！现在中国足球已经“山外青山楼外楼，场上跑着十一只大马猴”——过去是能力问题，现在纯来搞笑的。   国务院沦为军机处，李克强除了泄露“中国有六亿人月收入一千元”的机密，除了临死前那句“长江黄河不会倒流”，一事无成。   到了李强连军机处都不配，就是一个秉笔太监，开会时隔着大一截，生怕惊着圣驾。国务院组织法明确写上“拥护党中央领导”，政府立法宣布效忠政党，跟朝鲜没区别了，俄罗斯表面上宪法还规定“任何意识形态不得确立为国家强制性意识形态”。   宗教局也归并进党的统战部，信神，也归党管了。现在僧人做早课，念着念着就是：观自在菩萨，行深般若波罗蜜多时，照见五蕴皆空，树立两个确立、四个意识四个自信，坚决维护习近平党中央核心，政治意识、看齐意识，道路自信、制度自信……贫僧念的不是《金刚经》《心经》，而是党章和《习近平谈治国理政》。   这世道，没有高僧，只有妖僧。   枪杆子、钱袋子、印把子、木鱼子，刀把子，笔杆子是明确写出“习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想”，人还活着把思想挂上了自己名字，老江老胡没这待遇，老邓是死后才有这待遇，跟毛泽东并肩了。   只剩一关——老人。中共有老人政治，胡耀邦、赵紫阳都是被元老们批倒的。江泽民头上有邓小平，胡锦涛头上有江泽民。到了习近平，胡锦涛裸退，老江2022年去世……我翻遍历史，少见这么好运气的上位者。 看看活着的前政治局常委：   李岚清94岁，李瑞环92岁，罗干91岁，吴官正88岁，曾庆红87岁，胡锦涛84岁，温家宝84岁……   老人手里都没兵。除了胡锦涛温家宝曾庆红王岐山，都没政治影响力，有也是负的，跳出个张高丽，人们立马联想到女子网球运动。   重要的是造反这事儿是冲动型产业，上了年纪随着睾丸酮下降就造不动了。历史上除了司马懿70岁时发动高平陵之变，李世民玄武门之变才28岁，赵匡胤陈桥兵变才33岁，朱棣起兵靖难39岁，杨坚篡北周40岁，拿破仑雾月政变才30岁。年纪大了没心思反了。当初涛哥被拖出去，手下连目送都不敢，正可谓，问君能有几多愁，恰似一群太……太阳今儿真好啊。 content:
中国2026年前三季度结婚登记量持续下滑；人口学家预测，2027年的出生人数将暴跌
中国2026年前三季度结婚登记量持续下滑；人口学家预测，2027年的出生人数将暴跌
中国2026年前三季度结婚登记量持续下滑；人口学家预测，2027年的出生人数将暴跌
资料照片：在中国“十一”假期间，一位中国新娘在北京故宫附近拍摄婚纱照。(2021年10月3日)
中国民政部刚刚公布的数据显示：2026年前三季度，全国结婚登记仅有464.8万对。人口学家预测，这意味着2027年的出生人口将暴跌。
中国民政部星期四(11月5日)发布了《2026年3季度民政统计数据》报告。报告显示：2026年前三季度，中国全国结婚登记464.8万对，比上年同期减少50.4万对；从季度上看，第一季度与去年同比下降6.2%，第二季度下降8.7%，第三季度下降14.9%，三季度降幅明显扩大。
美国威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校人口统计学家易富贤在接受美国之音(VOA)采访时表示，这意味着2027年的出生人口数量将暴跌。
易富贤说：“因为结婚与下一年的出生数是高度相关的，这就意味着2027年的中国出生数会非常快速地下降。”
自2025年5月10日起，中国正式施行新修订的《婚姻登记条例》。该条例取消了婚姻登记的地域限制，大陆居民可以在全国任何一个县级以上婚姻登记机关办理结婚或离婚登记。同一年，中国全国依法办理结婚登记为676.51万对，比2024年610.6万对增长了大约10.8%。
易富贤表示，当时，很多人很高兴，认为中国政府终于遏制了结婚下降的趋势，必将带来出生人口的上升，但这其实只是政策变动带来的短期反弹而已。他解释说，放宽婚姻登记限制可以满足部分积压需求，就像以旧换新补贴可以提前释放消费需求一样。
易富贤告诉美国之音：“(中国)去年结婚数量增加了11%，今年的出生数也会有所增加，今年的出生数会提高到八百多万。但是由于今年的结婚数下降了10%，也就意味着明年的出生数将会下降，大概只有七百多万。”
易富贤表示，中国人口的一些结构性因素，比如适婚人口萎缩、初婚年龄推迟、生育意愿下降等等并未改变，因此，不能把短期政策效应误判为人口趋势的逆转。
民政部的统计数据还显示，中国第一季度至第三季度的离婚登记数量几乎保持不变，仅增加0.5万对，总数达到208.2万对。
中国是世界人口第二大国，但其人口老龄化速度很快。由于从1980年至2015年实行的的“一胎化(或称一孩)政策”、改革开放期间快速的城镇化，以及高企的房价、不稳定的就业市场和前景、高昂的育儿成本等因素，导致中国人结婚和育儿的意愿持续下降，中国的新生儿出生率近年来更是遭遇断崖式下降。这一趋势正在对中国社会的经济、家庭、医疗支出及公共服务等方方面面带来深远影响。
为了应对结婚率持续下降和人口快速萎缩的问题，近年来中国从中央到地方出台了一系列综合性政策与创新举措，其中包括婚姻登记“全国通办”、延长婚假、物质奖励、消费补贴等措施，但是仍然无法提升结婚数量。
长期研究中国人口问题的易富贤告诉美国之音，中国导致结婚减少、出生下降的原因很多，有众多短板，只有全部补齐才能提升生育率；但是中国政府到目前为止只是补了其中很少的几块，有些短板在哪里都不知道。
易富贤举例说，比如中国居民可支配收入占GDP比例太低，象2025年，中国居民可支配收入只占GDP的43%，远低于国际社会的60-70%，这样生育率很难稳定在1.0，更遑论提升。
易富贤指出，而中国要提高居民可支配收入占比，那便是个天大的难题。

content:
资料照片：苏黎世一家工厂建筑上的瑞士工程集团ABB的标志。
总部位于瑞士苏黎世的ABB集团星期四(11月5日)表示，中国政府已通知日本投资集团软银，反对其以约54亿美元收购ABB旗下在中国的机器人业务的交易。
ABB全球电气化和自动化领域的领先企业。该集团官网星期四公布的一份新闻稿中说表示，“ABB确认，软银已告知，中国外商投资安全审查工作机制办公室已禁止软银收购ABB机器人在中国的机器人业务。”声明还说，“ABB与软银正保持密切沟通，并积极推进交易事宜。”
2025年10月，ABB宣布签署协议，将旗下机器人业务部门以53.75亿美元出售给软银集团。不过，“交易尚需获得监管机构批准并满足惯例成交条件。监管审批流程由软银负责推进。”
这是近年来全球工业自动化和机器人领域最引人注目的并购交易。根据ABB中国，中国是ABB集团全球第二大市场。ABB近十年在华累计投资超过10亿美元，约85%的销售收入来源于本土制造的产品、系统和服务。目前，ABB在中国拥有研发、制造、销售和工程服务等业务活动，30家本地企业、1.4万名员工遍布于100余个城市。
中国外商投资安全审查工作机制办公室隶属中国国家发展和改革委员会。这是今年该办公室第二次阻止在中国的高科技企业被收购。
今年4月，中国外商投资安全审查工作办公室要求美国科技巨头Meta撤销对人工智能初创企业Manus逾20亿美元的收购。当时，该办公室宣布， “依法依规对外资收购Manus项目作出了禁止投资决定，”并要求双方撤回收购交易。
中国政府正大力度，防止本土科技企业将核心技术和知识产权转移至海外。
英国《金融时报》的报导称，直到上个星期，与软银关系密切的人士以及了解中国国家发展改革委相关流程的人士原本都曾预计，尽管该交易需接受外商投资安全审查，但仍会获得批准。该交易于2月份通过了中国的公平竞争审查。
11月5日，在中国外交部例行记者会上，中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆在被问到对相关问题时说，“这个问题建议向中方主管部门进行询问。”

content:
资料照片：英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在北京中国国际供应链博览会开幕式后，被媒体包围。(2025年7月16日)
路透社星期四(11月5日)披露，一批英伟达(Nvidia)的先进芯片由于北京未批准放行，目前仍滞留在香港。这凸显了尽管中国科技公司对芯片的需求强劲，美国也已经批准出口，但中国当局对芯片进口的“卡脖子”做法，成为这批英伟达芯片进入中国的主要障碍。
路透社援引知情人士的说法，大约有60万枚英伟达H200先进超级智能(通常称人工智能或AI)芯片，由于北京尚未批准进口，目前仍存放在香港，等待被运往中国。
报道指这些没有被报道过的H200芯片库存规模反映出，北京不愿意加深对美国先进技术的依赖。
英伟达芯片滞留香港凸显了中国当局的矛盾，一方面希望获得西方芯片的先进计算能力，以满足中国这个世界第二大经济体日益增加的超级智能需求。另一方面，又不希望过度依赖美国芯片，以保护本国芯片厂商。
今年5月，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)在台北表示，英伟达已经获得美国政府许可，可以向中国销售H200芯片，但仍未获得中国官员批准。
黄仁勋说，如果能够服务中国市场将是“极好的”，因为“中国市场非常重要，也非常大”。不过，华盛顿的放行并没有自动带来北京的接受。
分析人士指出，这一僵局凸显，美中的芯片竞争已不再只是华盛顿限制中国获取美国技术的问题，而越来越成为北京如何在获得先进算力与扶持国产替代之间取舍的问题。
路透社星期四的报道指出，最近几个月中国已经有限度的放行，让部分芯片进入中国。但几家主要的中国互联网公司仅各自获得了大约1万枚H200芯片，与这些企业庞大的超级智能模型训练刚需相比，只能说是杯水车薪。
位在首都华盛顿的人工智能政策与战略研究院(IAPS)研究员徐森凯(Karson Elmgren)在X上发文表示，中国的做法确实让人难以理解。
“有点难理解为什么中国对于进口大家认为是我们这个时代*技术工业革命*的原材料如此谨慎。在我看来，这表明他们不认为短期优势至关重要，而且对自己中期的替代能力很有信心。”他说。
彼得森国际经济研究所(Peterson Institute for International Economics)高级研究员马永哲(Martin Chorzempa)也表示同意。
“他们(中国)认为国内芯片设计师/生产商的推进要比短期能力更重要，但我也觉得基于基准测试的有限能力差距让北京对实验室关于短缺阻碍发展的抱怨有所质疑。”
今年5月，美国贸易代表贾米森·格里尔(Jamieson Greer)在一场公开座谈会上，谈到了英伟达芯片销售在中国遇阻的原因。“中国企业对英伟达H200芯片感兴趣，但中国共产党更关注推动国产芯片发展。”他说。
路透社报道，因为供应受限，一些中国买家转而通过中介和间接渠道购买，推高了非官方市场的价格。一位知情人士表示，截至10月底，一台八卡H200服务器在中国的报价超过600万元人民币(约90万美元)，大约是一年前价格的三倍。这名人士还表示，采用英伟达更新的Blackwell芯片且受美国出口管制的服务器，单台报价更超过2000万元人民币。
报道指出，在中国官方极度锁紧进口配额的情况下，中国的科技买家被迫走非官方途径，直接推高了地下黑市的价格。
美国之音就英伟达先进芯片滞留香港一事向美国贸易代表办公室、商务部以及英伟达公司发出置评请求，截至报道发表前，尚未收到回应。
美国官员指控中国“月之暗面”窃取Anthropic模型，并称其获取受限的英伟达芯片

content:
中国国家主席习近平和对中国进行国事访问的阿曼苏丹海赛姆·本·塔里克·阿勒赛义德，在北京人民大会堂出席欢迎仪式。(2026年11月2日)
在美国对伊朗持续进行有限度打击之际，中国高调发动外交行动介入斡旋。北京这个月将派遣特使前往中东，试图推动对话并缓解地区紧张局势。观察人士指出，中国在中东影响力虽有所增长，不过要斡旋止战却是心有余而力不足，充其量只能营造出一个空泛的和平促进者形象。
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)星期二(11月３日)证实，美军星期一晚间对伊朗格什姆岛(Qeshm Island)发动“小规模袭击”。《华尔街日报》援引美国官员的话报道，此次打击是近几周一系列有限度、有针对性的打击行动之一。
美军执行打击前一刻，中国国家主席习近平在北京会晤首次对中国进行国事访问的阿曼苏丹海赛姆·本·塔里克·阿勒赛义德(Haitham Bin Tariq Al-Said)。
据联合声明，阿曼支持习近平先后提出的一系列致力于中东和平稳定的倡议和主张，期待中国为实现中东长治久安发挥更大作用。
声明也提到，双方呼吁坚持通过政治外交途径化解争端，尽早实现全面停火止战，达成包括核问题在内的全面协议；双方认为霍尔木兹海峡应恢复正常、安全通航。
中国外交部发言人毛宁星期一于例行记者会上指出，中国中东问题特使翟雋以及非洲事务特别代表刘显法将于11月上中旬分赴地区国家穿梭访问，旨在“劝和促谈、缓局降温，为维护地区和平稳定发挥建设性作用”。
北京是德黑兰的重要盟友，也是伊朗原油的最大买家。与此同时，中国高度依赖经霍尔木兹海峡运输的能源，长期冲突可能干扰航运及供应链。
《华盛顿邮报》星期三报道称随着中东局势可能进入更危险阶段，中方领导层正试图在决定区域未来走向的过程中取得一席之地，并将自身塑造成维护稳定的力量。
华盛顿智库中东问题研究所中东-亚洲项目主任约翰·卡拉布莱斯(John Calabrese)指出，北京仍沿用惯用策略，也就是呼吁各方保持克制、支持停火并援引国际法，并将自己定位为对话的潜在推动者。
他认为，2023年在中国斡旋下达成的沙乌地阿拉伯-伊朗和解，虽然彰显出北京外交作用的影响力，也揭露了其局限。
卡拉布莱斯通过电邮向美国之音表示：“促进外交对话与成为可信的和平斡旋者之间存在着巨大的鸿沟。”
他解释道，在双方都希望缓和局势的政治背景下，中国所惯用的和解机制或许有效；一旦地区紧张局势从外交层面转向军事对抗，缺乏强制力的斡旋就难以保证。
卡拉布莱斯强调，北京虽然扩大其在中东的影响力，并与各方建立了联系，但它既缺乏足够的筹码，也缺乏承担有效调解所带来的风险和责任的意愿。“作为调解人尚且能力不足，更遑论安全保障者。”
观察人士说，促进和平调解的重要筹码之一是斡旋方本身的军事存在，但是中国既不愿被卷入冲突，在中东也不具备威慑力量，因此对该地区安全保障的能力十分有限。
位于台北的国防安全研究院副研究员黄恩浩指出，中国目前是采“搭便车”策略，也就是由美国海军安全体系来保护国际能源航线。换言之，中国不愿承担区域安全的沉重成本，只有在条件成熟时推一把，其行为趋近于“半调解”。
尽管北京被指控给予伊朗军事上的支持，包括导弹与军工技术转移，以及情报与卫星支援，然而在中东缺乏军事存在是不争事实。
黄恩浩告诉美国之音：“(斡旋)施力会相当有限，因为它(中国)基本上外交政策是不干涉它国内政，再来就是说它在中东地区就是输出一些投资、基础设施甚至是一带一路的一些项目，所以基本上它还是以经贸外交为主，在安全部分，主导的还是美国、以色列。”
美国之音就中国派遣特使前往中东调停一事向美国国务院和白宫发出置评请求，至报道发表前，还未收到回应。
位于台北的政治大学外交学系教授李登科接受美国之音采访时表示，北京是真心希望能够扮演斡旋者的角色。如果斡旋成功不仅提升国际形象，更能确保其经济利益，然而问题在于中国没办法满足美伊双方的条件。
自2月底中东战事爆发以来，历经多轮交火与短暂停火协议破裂。美国坚持霍尔木兹海峡必须立即、无条件开放，并彻底限制伊朗核计划。
伊朗国家安全委员会秘书穆赫辛·雷扎伊(Mohsen Rezaei)星期二重申，美方必须完整、明确回应伊朗提出的7项条件；这些条件包括取消石油制裁、结束美国海上封锁，以及解冻伊朗被冻结的资金。
李登科说：“它(中国)有兴趣介入是一回事，能不能介入又是一回事。那当然表面上美国不会去拒绝，只是说你要美国同意(停火)的话，美国可能要求中国说，你要介入这个斡旋或调解没有问题，但是你一定要让伊朗接受我的条件，那这个(中国)做不到嘛。”
李登科进一步指出，中国不仅没有能力调停美伊之间的战事，就连伊朗与周边阿拉伯国家的冲突，恐怕也是束手无策。
习近平在会晤阿曼苏丹海赛姆时表示，中东和海湾地区不应成为大国竞争的战场，中国愿与阿拉伯国家共同努力，实现持久和平。
包括阿曼在内，沙特阿拉伯、卡达、阿联酋、巴林及科威特等海湾国家，在美伊战争期间皆曾遭伊朗袭击。中国虽然是伊朗坚定盟友，同时也和这些阿拉伯国家保持密切关系。
李登科指出，海湾地区的阿拉伯国家因为有美军基地，所以成为伊朗的打击目标，而这也是伊朗“以战止战”的筹码。从德黑兰政权的角度而言，没道理放着这个杀手锏不用，毕竟中国所能给予的安全保障仍比不上自身的吓阻力。

( printed page 69953) Notice of November 3, 2026
Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to the Threat From Securities Investments That Finance Certain Companies of the People's Republic of China
On November 12, 2020, by Executive Order 13959, the President declared a national emergency pursuant to the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) to deal with the unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economy of the United States constituted by the threat from securities investments that finance certain companies of the People's Republic of China (PRC).
The President found that the PRC is increasingly exploiting United States capital to resource and enable the development and modernization of its military, intelligence, and other security apparatuses, which continues to allow the PRC to directly threaten the United States homeland and United States forces overseas. Through the national strategy of Military-Civil Fusion, the PRC increases the size of the country's military-industrial complex by compelling civilian Chinese companies to support its military and intelligence activities. Those companies, though remaining ostensibly private and civilian, directly support the PRC's military, intelligence, and security apparatuses and aid in their development and modernization. At the same time, those companies raise capital by selling securities to United States investors that trade on public exchanges both here and abroad, lobbying United States index providers and funds to include these securities in market offerings, and engaging in other acts to ensure access to United States capital.
The President further found that the PRC's military-industrial complex, by directly supporting the efforts of the PRC's military, intelligence, and other security apparatuses, constituted an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economy of the United States.
On January 13, 2021, the President signed Executive Order 13974 amending Executive Order 13959.
On June 3, 2021, the President signed Executive Order 14032, which expanded the scope of the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13959. The President found that additional steps were necessary to address that national emergency, including the threat posed by the military-industrial complex of the PRC and its involvement in military, intelligence, and security research and development programs, and weapons and related equipment production under the PRC's Military-Civil Fusion strategy. In addition, the President found that the use of Chinese surveillance technology outside the PRC and the development or use of Chinese surveillance technology to facilitate repression or serious human rights abuse constituted unusual and extraordinary threats to the national security, foreign policy, and economy of the United States. Executive Order 14032 amended Executive Order 13959 and revoked Executive Order 13974 in its entirety.
The threat from securities investments that finance certain companies of the PRC and certain uses and development of Chinese surveillance technology continue to pose an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economy of the United States.
For this reason, the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13959 of November 12, 2020, expanded in scope by Executive Order 14032 of ( printed page 69954) June 3, 2021, must continue in effect beyond November 12, 2026. Therefore, in accordance with section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1622(d)), I am continuing for 1 year the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13959 with respect to the threat from securities investments that finance certain companies of the PRC and expanded in Executive Order 14032.
This notice shall be published in the Federal Register and transmitted to the Congress.

Legal Services Corporation.
Notice of proposed rulemaking.
This proposed rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC) definition of “capital improvement” by removing the threshold amount of LSC funds that must be expended on an improvement to real estate for the expenditure to qualify as a capital improvement. The proposed amendment would distinguish the definition of a capital improvement from the monetary thresholds required for prior approval; promote consistent tracking and oversight of LSC funds used for capital improvements; and strengthen accountability for LSC funds invested in recipients' real property.
Comments must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. Eastern on December 21, 2026.
You may submit comments by any of the following methods:
Email: lscrulemaking@lsc.gov. Include “Comments on Revision to Part 1631” in the subject line of the message.
Mail: Brittany Sims Nwankwoala, Assistant General Counsel, Legal Services Corporation, 1825 I St. NW, Ste. 800, Washington, DC 20006, ATTN: Part 1631 Rulemaking. ( printed page 69767)
Hand Delivery/Courier: Brittany Sims Nwankwoala, Assistant General Counsel, Legal Services Corporation, 1825 I St. NW, Ste. 800, Washington, DC 20006, ATTN: Part 1631 Rulemaking.
Instructions: Electronic submissions are preferred via email with attachments in Acrobat PDF format. LSC will not consider written comments sent to any other address or received after the end of the comment period.
Brittany Sims Nwankwoala, Assistant General Counsel, Legal Services Corporation, 1825 I St. NW, Ste. 800, Washington, DC 20006; (202) 295-1599 (phone), or nwankwoalab@lsc.gov.
The Legal Services Corporation Act of 1974 authorizes LSC to establish regulations governing the use of grant funds and to ensure appropriate stewardship of Federal resources. See 42 U.S.C. 2996g(e). LSC sets forth its procurement and property management requirements in 45 CFR part 1631.
In 2017, LSC revised parts 1630, pertaining to cost standards, and 1631 to increase the prior approval threshold from $10,000 to $25,000 to account for inflation and reduce unnecessary administrative burdens on recipients. This change also established $25,000 as the applicable threshold in all provisions governing prior approval, property, and procurement requirements. In 2022, LSC conducted a retrospective review of all regulations. It identified several additional areas within parts 1630 and 1631 that recipients and LSC staff found difficult to administer consistently or that lacked sufficient clarity for grantees and oversight staff. In 2026, LSC initiated rulemaking to resolve those inconsistencies and increase the $25,000 prior approval threshold to $50,000 in §§ 1630.3, 1630.6, 1631.8, and 1631.15. See 91 FR 23228 (Apr. 30, 2026).
During the 2026 rulemaking, however, LSC did not propose increasing the threshold in the definition of “capital improvement” in § 1631.2(a). Although LSC increased the threshold for obtaining prior approval for certain expenditures from $25,000 to $50,000, that amendment would not address which expenditures constitute capital improvements for purposes of part 1631. Rather, through subsequent conversations with the Office of Compliance Enforcement (OCE), LSC found that removing the threshold amount altogether would enhance LSC's ability to identify and account for all LSC funds used to improve real property. Currently, expenditures below the threshold may nevertheless constitute capital improvements and, when repeatedly made over time, could represent a significant investment of LSC funds in a recipient's real property. The $50,000 threshold for determining when prior approval is required remains separate from the definition of “capital improvement.”
II. Remove the Threshold Amount in Definition of Capital Improvement
LSC proposes to revise the definition of “capital improvement” in § 1631.2(a) by removing any monetary threshold from the definition. Currently, § 1631.2(a) defines “capital improvement” as spending more than $50,000 of LSC funds to improve real estate through construction or the addition of fixtures that become an integral part of the real estate. LSC proposes to remove the monetary threshold so that any improvement to real estate using LSC funds constitutes a capital improvement.
LSC is undertaking this rulemaking to strengthen its oversight of LSC funds used to improve real property and ensure that recipients identify and account for such expenditures regardless of amount. The amendment also clarifies that an expenditure may constitute a capital improvement even if it does not meet the monetary threshold requiring LSC's prior approval. The character of an expenditure made with LSC funds as a capital improvement does not depend on its cost. An expenditure may improve real estate through construction or the addition of an integral fixture even when the amount of LSC funds used for that particular improvement is less than the applicable prior approval threshold.
Removing the monetary threshold from the definition would also ensure that recipients identify and account for any LSC funds used for capital improvements regardless of the amount of the individual expenditure. Under the current definition, improvements costing less than $50,000 do not constitute “capital improvements” for purposes of part 1631. As a result, a recipient could make multiple improvements to the same real estate over time using LSC funds, with each individual improvement falling below $50,000, without those expenditures being treated as capital improvements under the rule. For example, a recipient could expend $30,000 of LSC funds on an improvement in one year and later expend an additional $40,000 on another improvement to the same property in a different year. Although the recipient would have invested a total of $70,000 of LSC funds in improvements to the property, neither expenditure would constitute a capital improvement under the current definition.
This result is inconsistent with LSC's interest in ensuring that recipients accurately identify and account for LSC funds invested in real estate. Section 1631.15(c) requires recipients to maintain supporting documentation sufficient to accurately identify and account for any use of LSC funds to make capital improvements to real estate owned by the recipient. Removing the $50,000 threshold from the definition would make the definition consistent with that requirement and enable LSC and recipients to account for the cumulative amount of LSC funds invested in improvements to real estate over time.
The proposed amendment would also clarify the distinction between the classification and tracking of an expenditure and the requirement to obtain prior approval. Removing the dollar amount from the definition of “capital improvement” would not, by itself, require prior approval for every capital improvement. Rather, grantees would need to treat and track expenditures that meet the definition as a capital improvement regardless of amount. Meanwhile, the applicable provisions governing prior approval would continue to determine when a recipient must obtain LSC's approval before using LSC funds for the improvement.
This change would ensure that the regulatory definition accurately identifies the nature of the expenditure and that LSC's interest in real estate reflects LSC funds used for capital improvements, including improvements made through multiple expenditures over time.
PART 1631—PURCHASING AND PROPERTY MANAGEMENT
LSC proposes to revise the definition of “capital improvement” in § 1631.2(a) by removing the monetary amount of LSC funds a recipient may spend to improve real property through construction or the addition of fixtures that become an integral part of the real property.
For the reasons set forth in the preamble, the Legal Services Corporation proposes to amend part 1631 of title 45 of the Code of Federal Regulations as follows:
PART 1631—PURCHASING AND PROPERTY MANAGEMENT
1. The authority citation for part 1631 continues to read as follows:
Authority: 42 U.S.C. 2996g(e).
2. Amend § 1631.2 by revising paragraph (a) to read as follows:
(a) Capital improvement means spending any amount of LSC funds to improve real estate through construction or the addition of fixtures that become an integral part of real estate.
Deputy General Counsel and Ethics Officer, Legal Services Corporation.

Congo-Kinshasa: New DR Congo Rebel Coalition Threatens Radio Station, to Vet Broadcasts
Former Congolese President Joseph Kabila signing the documents formalising the creation of the Front for the Rebuilding of the Nation (FRN), a political and military movement, on 12 October 2026 in Goma, in the east of the DRC.
Committee to Protect Journalists (New York)
Kinshasa — The Committee to Protect Journalists urges the leaders of the new rebel movement, the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), to ensure the safety of journalist Guillaume Munguakonkwa, stop censoring Kamole FM, and allow media outlets to cover news freely and independently.
On October 16, six FRN rebels, accompanied by Colbert Jean-Baptiste Karume Kajabika, the Walungu Territory administrator's representative in the town of Nyangezi, in the eastern DRC province of South Kivu, burst into community radio station Kamole FM searching for its news presenter Munguakonkwa, station director Floribert Bayongwa, told CPJ. The group wanted to tell Munguakonkwa to broadcast their announcement inviting residents to an FRN meeting in Nyangezi that day, said Bayongwa, who witnessed the event.
At 10 a.m. that day and on October 15, Munguakonkwa had broadcast Karume's announcements, reviewed by CPJ, calling on locals to take part in cleanup activities and attend an FRN meeting. But the October 16 meeting was disrupted when government-aligned Wazalendo militia started shooting, so the rebels wanted to announce another one, Munguakonkwa told CPJ.
The journalist said he went into hiding for five days after Bayongwa warned him that the rebels were looking for him.
Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines
"The director quickly alerted me by phone, advising me to go into hiding and switch my phone to airplane mode," Munguakonkwa said. "At the same time, I received a message from an unknown number warning me to take cover, as armed individuals were reportedly looking for me."
"Since then, I have been living in constant fear, not knowing what steps to take to ensure my safety," he told CPJ. "I fear that I may face military reprisals from one side or the other, simply for having carried out my professional duties."
"Nothing can justify the threats made against journalist Guillaume Munguakonkwa or the directives imposed by FRN rebels on Kamole FM," said CPJ Africa Director Angela Quintal. "Throughout the conflict in the eastern DRC, journalists have faced physical and psychological threats, arrests, and death. All warring parties must recognize that access to information is of critical importance in situations of conflict."
On October 29, Karume summoned Bayongwa to his office and criticized the station for not covering the FRN meeting. Karume ordered him to submit all news intended for broadcast to his office for approval or else he would be imprisoned, the journalist told CPJ.
On October 12, former DRC President Joseph Kabila announced the formation of the FRN, which includes the M23 and Congo River Alliance (AFC) rebel movements that control much of eastern DRC.
On July 27, Munguakonkwa was detained for three days in an M23/AFC intelligence unit cell for reporting on the Ebola virus. His voice recorder, cell phone, and notebook were confiscated.

Unpacking the rebuttal for the appeal to the Cape Town Municipal Planning Tribunal approval for the Equinix data centres near the airport raises more questions than answers.
Illustrative image: A data centre in Ashburn, Virginia, United States. Housing developments there will soon be walled in by data centres, exemplifying the tensions over their unfettered growth. (Photo: Charles A Fazio / Bloomberg via Getty Images) | Cape Town skyline. (Photo: Gallo Images / Foto24 / Michael Hammond) | (By Daniella Lee Ming Yesca)
Getting one thing straight about the data centres planned for opposite Cape Town International Airport is that the developer on record, which is handling all the wheeling and dealing and issued the formal response to the appeal, is a crowd called Planning Partners.
They’re acting on behalf of King Air Industria (KAI, which is co-developed by Atterbury) and Equinix. According to the 91-page response that could be obtained only via a Paia request, which Daily Maverick has now studied, Equinix’s involvement in the KAI project centres on a long-term commercial lease and infrastructure funding arrangement.
Crucially, Equinix’s legal counsel (Baker & McKenzie) advised the company not to proceed with multi-hundred-million-rand investments unless the City of Cape Town provided explicit statutory certainty that data centres are legally permitted under municipal zoning rules. This legal warning directly prompted the City to amend its Municipal Planning By-law to explicitly include “data centre” under the definition of a warehouse.
Now that we’re all on the same page, we can dive into the primary defence.
Planning Partners argues that the objectors misunderstand municipal planning law under Item 136 of the Development Management Scheme.
They state that, under this framework, large precincts are developed in stages. The developer contends that the current application merely subdivides, consolidates and rezones land to create a buildable site (Erf 180451 for Data Centre 2).
The argument is that granular operational details – such as building architecture, cooling mechanics, noise propagation, fuel storage and National Environmental Management Act (Nema) environmental triggers – belong strictly to the subsequent Site Development Plan and Building Plan stages.
But while co-developer Atterbury publicly described the application as an “inconsequential” 280m² boundary correction and claimed Equinix’s involvement was purely speculative, the appeal response submitted by Planning Partners explicitly confirms Equinix as the primary party driving the development.
“In August, Equinix’s South Africa MD said there was a ‘misnomer’ in the public perception of data centres’ consumption of critical resources,” Daniel Hartford, the South African lead for UK legal advocacy non-profit Foxglove, explained in response to Daily Maverick’s questions about the rebuttal.
Foxglove and the Legal Resources Centre (LRC) made the Paia request for the document after the City decided to handle the appeal hearing behind closed doors.
“Since then, his company’s response to Foxglove’s appeal has been revealed. It confirms – despite repeated denials to the press – that Equinix is indeed behind the planning application. It says this in black and white on the second page of Equinix’s appeal response. When the audience was the City, the site was Equinix’s data centre. When the audience was journalists and the public, it was 280 square metres of nothing in particular.”
In October 2024, the City approved the site for the first data centre (Erf 180444) under General Industry 1 (GI1) zoning. At the time, the Development Management Scheme contained no mention or definition of a “data centre”. As Daily Maverick reported previously, the City treated data centres as a primary permitted right under General Industry 1 by interpreting digital data as “goods stored in a warehouse”.
In 2025, Baker & McKenzie and senior counsel challenged this interpretation. They advised Equinix that categorising a data centre as a warehouse storing physical goods would not withstand legal scrutiny under standard statutory interpretation.
Equinix formally notified the City that due to the multi-hundred-million-rand investment required, it would not proceed with the development without explicit statutory legal certainty.
Data centre deal — Cape Town forced back to the drawing board
To resolve the legal concerns, the City initiated an amendment to the Municipal Planning By-law (read: Development Management Scheme). Passed by Council on 26 June 2026 and coming into full operation on 1 October 2026, the amendment inserted explicit definitions into municipal law:
Definition of ‘data centre’: “ ‘data centre’ means a building or dedicated space within a building or a group of buildings used to store computer systems and associated components, such as telecommunication and storage systems;”
Amended definition of ‘warehouse’: “ ‘Warehouse’ means a building used primarily for the storage of goods, except those that are offensive or dangerous, and includes property used for a data centre or a business of a retail or wholesale nature;”
Amended definition of ‘business premises’: Explicitly updated to include “data centre” alongside shops and offices.
By linking “data centre” directly into the definitions of “warehouse” and “business premises”, data centres automatically now became a primary permitted right across all General Industry (GI1) and Mixed Use (MU1) properties city-wide without requiring individual rezoning or consent use approvals.
Wait, but what is the City’s stance?
Good question. Upon reviewing the evidence and gleaning conversations with the main characters in Geordin Hill-Lewis’ administration, the City of Cape Town is operating under an investor-focused “open for business” agenda, seeking to establish the metro as Africa’s premier digital hub. To secure hyperscale tech investments, the City has demonstrated extreme responsiveness – amending municipal planning laws, facilitating land swaps, and accepting upfront infrastructure contributions.
From an administrative perspective, it seems to be a done deal. Why? Because the record shows that:
The City has already accepted R33.3-million in Shared Network Charges from Equinix.
The executive mayor signed off on the underlying land swap in May 2026.
The City proactively altered its Municipal Planning By-law specifically to remove legal hurdles raised by Equinix’s attorneys.
The City has shielded Equinix’s appeal submissions from public scrutiny and held appeal advisory hearings in private.
The City has already approved five data centres across the metro, with two more under assessment.
The wildest disclosure in the 91-page rebuttal, however, is how it deals with the environmental authorisation (EA) and water usage rights.
KAI received an environmental authorisation from the Western Cape Department of Environmental Affairs and Development Planning on 11 May 2018 for a generic mixed-use industrial park.
The project Environmental Assessment Practitioner (Chand Consultants) asserts that data centres fit inside this broad baseline envelope.
A new Nema Environmental Impact Assessment will only be triggered at the Site Development Plan stage if detailed designs exceed specific thresholds – such as backup diesel generator capacity exceeding 10MW under Listing Notice 2.
KAI holds a General Authorisation issued under Section 21(c) and 21(i) of the National Water Act on 15 March, 2018 for watercourse and wetland alterations. The Environmental Assessment Practitioner confirms that constructing the data centres remains within this General Authorisation scope and requires no new Water Use License Application.
The developer argues that detailed environmental, water, and energy assessments belong strictly to the future Site Development Plan stage under a “Package of Plans” framework. The Legal Resources Centre (LRC) counters that deferring these critical studies leaves communities unprotected while offering no legally binding commitments on green energy or water security.
“On cooling and renewables it contradicts itself: air-source cooling is ‘confirmed’ and ‘not yet finalised’; renewable PPAs are ‘confirmed’ and ‘will be decided upon at a later date’… Nothing binds the applicant,” was what the LRC had to say in response to Daily Maverick’s inquiry.
Following the conclusion of the appeal panel hearing, the appellants are awaiting the final ruling from the Appeal Authority (none other than City of Cape Town Executive Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis).
The LRC says that it is now focusing on the appeals process. Once a decision has been made, they will consider their options and determine the most appropriate route to take the matter forward.
One option may involve a review challenge in the high court under Paja [Promotion of Administrative Justice Act]. However, their approach will depend on the decision of the mayor and other circumstances at that stage.
“South Africa needs a discussion about digital infrastructure: about why it is needed, who it is for, who will pay the cost and how it will affect us,” says Foxglove’s Hartford.
“It is disappointing that instead of being transparent about its plans... Equinix has chosen – through omission and contradiction – to deepen the very confusion it has complained about publicly. Capetonians deserve better.” DM
