The New York Times reportedly in talks to buy Letterboxd for $330 million
The New York Times Company has reportedly “entered exclusive negotiations” to acquire Letterboxd for $330 million, according to a report from The New York Times itself.
Letterboxd, an online platform for movie lovers that could be compared to Goodreads for movies, has grown dramatically in recent years. Letterboxd reported 3 million users in January 2021, a figure that grew to 28 million by April of this year. More than half of its users are under 35.
Letterboxd was previously reported to be seeking a new owner. According to the Times, film studios A24 and Sony were interested in the acquisition, but A24 was priced out.
Letterboxd is free, but users can access advanced features with a paid subscription. Its projected earnings for this year are estimated at $15 million, which is only about 4.5% of what the Times is supposedly offering to buy the company for.
The New York Times Company declined to comment on the acquisition to its own paper (lol). Personally, we wouldn’t be surprised if these anonymous tips were coming from inside the house, so we’re inclined to take this report pretty seriously.

Meta, Google, and TikTok sue California AG over teen social media law
4:01 PM PST · November 5, 2026
Meta, Google, and TikTok have each filed lawsuits against California Attorney General Rob Bonta in an attempt to block a law that restricts social media features it deems addictive for users under 16.
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed the bill, known as AB 1709, into law in September, and it’s slated to take effect at the start of the new year.
The law prohibits social platforms from offering autoplay videos and personalized feeds to users under 16, and it requires the platforms to delete these users’ accounts if they don’t turn those features off. If platforms do not comply, they could be liable for fines of up to $50,000 per affected user under 16 years old.
Meta claims that AB 1709 violates the First Amendment by overriding its editorial decisions about how to display content, adding that Section 230 preempts the law. TikTok and Google made similar arguments.
“Meta currently organizes its feeds of content to include personalized content recommendations and to automatically play media, [so] the Act would make it unlawful for Meta to disseminate speech to minors altogether, and would require Meta to delete minors’ accounts, unless it changes these practices,” the company wrote in its lawsuit.
In an emailed statement, a TikTok spokesperson added, “AB 1709 is a blatantly unconstitutional restriction on free expression that erodes the long-standing and protected practice of curating content based on user preferences, which book stores, TV networks and streaming services all use.”
AB 1709 follows a trend of legislation around the world that seeks to curb teen social media use in an attempt to improve teen mental health outcomes. However, digital safety experts often caution against these laws because they can inadvertently compromise the privacy of all platform users, including adults, by requiring age verification checks that collect more user data.
“AB 1709 compels platforms to collect even more information from every user, invading everyone’s privacy and frustrating our ability to remain anonymous online,” EFF Associate Director of State Affairs Rindala Alajaji said in a press briefing. “Online surveillance by social media companies is harmful, and yet this bill requires even more of it, further concentrating power in the hands of tech companies rather than actually protecting users.”
Alajaji added that teenagers’ use of social media has been instrumental in enabling impactful digital activism, citing the Parkland shooting survivors’ March for Our Lives and climate activist Greta Thunberg’s global reach.
“As a functional ban on social media for youth under 16, AB 1709 cuts young people off from essential information and experiences, silencing the very voices it claims to protect,” Alajaji said.
These platforms are primed to fight this California law as they navigate similar legal battles in various countries. That’s especially true for Meta, which agreed to pay a settlement of up to $18 billion to resolve children’s safety claims brought by 29 U.S. states.
In December 2025, Australia became the first country to ban social media for users under 16 altogether. France passed a similar law, but its top court struck it down, citing concerns about violations of free expression rights.
These platforms also argue that the law would affect parents’ ability to make decisions about their teens’ internet use through parental controls.
A Google spokesperson noted that autoplay on YouTube is turned off for minors by default, and that parents have the ability to turn off their teens’ access to Shorts altogether.
“We believe parents are best positioned to make the right decisions for their families, which is why we offer a range of protections and tools that put parents in control,” a Google spokesperson said. “Overly broad laws like this actually break the systems we’ve built to help kids find high-quality, age-appropriate videos.”
A representative for Attorney General Bonta said that his office is reviewing the filings and is committed to “defending California’s commonsense laws to protect kids online.”

Airbnb says it’s launching an AI travel agent in the first half of 2027
2:40 PM PST · November 5, 2026
Airbnb has teased its plans to build its own AI travel agent before, but on Thursday the company announced that the new AI feature will launch in the first half of 2027. In the company’s Q3 shareholder letter on Thursday, Airbnb also provided more detail about how the agent will work, what it will actually do, and how it’s different from a typical AI chatbot.
In prior interviews, CEO Brian Chesky sketched out the travel company’s approach to AI, describing a plan to build an AI agent that has a richer interface than a conventional chatbot. He also expressed his opinions about how chatbots aren’t the right interface for travel, noting that people take pleasure in the planning process and in anticipating a trip. Any agent that it built, then, shouldn’t take away from the inspiration and the browsing, he told TechCrunch in an interview last month.
Chesky today reiterated that belief, telling analysts on the earnings call that people won’t use one AI agent for everything.
“Today’s AI agents like Muse and Instinct are good at simple routine tasks like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment. But planning a trip is different,” he said. “Travel is aspirational. Discovering where to go and where to stay is part of the experience. In fact, 80% of travelers say they enjoy spending time researching trips. People want to look at photos. They want to compare homes. They want to make decisions with people they’re traveling with,” he continued. “And I don’t think the general-purpose agents are the best to do that. So that is why we are building our own AI agent,” Chesky said.
Airbnb described its agent as having a personalized interface that’s designed specifically for travel, where it will “build an interface” around a user’s question instead of simply responding as a chatbot would.
“What we are doing is developing a custom-designed AI-native experience that responds to what guests are looking for,” Chesky said. “So instead of relying on traditional chat alone, which is very text-heavy — which, again, is definitely not the way you should plan travel, our agent draws from a library of hundreds of travel-specific interface components — maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, itineraries — and composes them in real time to match what they’re looking for.”
The exec said the agent will feel “a little bit like generative UI” as it’s designed to offer up “the right interface at the right time” for someone’s specific travel needs.
In its shareholder letter, the company touted that its nearly 20 years of experience in bringing hosts and guests together is informing how the agent is built, as it incorporates insights about how people both book and host on its platform. The agent will also be able to help travelers beyond the booking itself.
“Our agent will be able to help guests throughout their trip — from changing a reservation or resolving a payment issue to getting help with refunds, rebooking, or 24-hour safety support. These are things an outside agent can’t easily do on its own,” the company wrote.
Over time, Airbnb expects the agent will be able to help travelers with other aspects of their trip, including not only homes and hotels, but also services and experiences. Services and experiences are two areas that have become a bigger focus for the company following its redesign last year.
While the company previously said to expect its AI agent sometime in the next year, it’s now more specifically committing to roll out the new technology to consumers in the first half of 2027.
The news of the agent’s release was delivered alongside strong third-quarter earnings, with revenue growing 19% to $4.87 billion, topping Wall Street estimates. It also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast, which it now predicts will be in the high teens, instead of the mid-teens.
“Airbnb is back in growth mode,” Chesky told analysts on the Q3 earnings call on Thursday. “It’s rare for a marketplace of our size to reaccelerate growth, but that’s exactly what we’re doing. Q3 was our fastest revenue growth in more than three years,” he added.

Meta warns that election backlash against data centers could make AI expansion harder
11:12 AM PST · November 5, 2026
Meta president Dina Powell McCormick said that the Democratic wins in the midterm elections are going to make it a lot harder for companies to build data centers, adding that the industry has “not done as good a job as we needed to explain the benefits of these investments.”
Speaking at the WSJ Tech conference on Wednesday, the Meta exec pointed out that the backlash against data centers — which was very much on the ballot during this election season — was also tied to people’s feelings about AI technology overall.
“The visible sort of manifestation of AI is a data center, and it’s something that people can say, ‘I don’t want this in my community,’” she explained. “I think there’s an underlying bigger issue, which is how people feel about AI in general.”
Meta believes it could turn around the negative consumer sentiment around AI if it’s able to demonstrate the value, not only of the data centers coming to local communities, but also in the technology itself.
“The stakes of who builds the technology that cures cancer, that gives access to education, that is also a very fundamental difference … Mark [Zuckerberg, Meta CEO] is very ‘long human,’ and he’s betting on humans more than machines,” Powell McCormick explained. “And that’s what we mean when we say the future is for everyone. That people should not be left behind. But the way to ensure that is that this technology is democratized, that people have access to it in a very fair and transparent way,” she said.
The exec also touted Meta’s experience in building data centers, saying that the company has been doing so for 20 years, as it takes a lot of compute power to offer the products it does in the social networking space. Today, the company has data centers in 23 states, she said, and five of them, including one in Texas, are planned as projects of 1 gigawatt or more.
But Meta is now worried that it could lose some of its investments after politicians ran on anti-data-center platforms during the midterms.
“I think it’s going to be harder,” Powell McCormick said, describing what the future of building data centers looks like. “It has been hard, I should say, but I also think that it’s becoming clear what models work, and the states want those models that work.”
Specifically, communities only want data centers when it benefits them in some way, she explained, laying out the approach that Meta today uses to close its data center deals in local communities.
Successful projects see Meta paying for its own electricity, directing any tax surpluses as a result of the data centers toward teachers and first responders, keeping the labor force local, and getting bipartisan support for the project, among other things.
Going forward, she expects data center projects to come under more review and be weighed against whether the constituents actually want them.
Meta has pinned its hopes on its AI investments, particularly its consumer AI agent Muse scaling far beyond the 10 million users it has today, to become a business that one day serves billions. But even if that’s not the case, it believes that its investments in data centers will not be for nothing, as the compute itself will be valuable.
“We’re getting calls every day to lease that compute [we’ve built], and so one way or another, we’re seeing a path to monetization,” Powell McCormick said.

Claude can now analyze your spending with its new Personal Finance tool
10:00 AM PST · November 5, 2026
Anthropic announced Thursday that Claude is getting a new tool called “Personal Finance,” designed to help users keep track of their money. With it, users can connect their bank and credit card accounts through Plaid and ask Claude questions about their finances. Anthropic says access is read-only, meaning Personal Finance can’t move, manage, or invest users’ money.
By letting Claude connect directly to bank and credit card accounts, Anthropic is positioning its chatbot as a financial companion that can help people understand their spending and make sense of their money, rather than simply offering them generic advice.
With the launch, Claude is playing catch-up to OpenAI’s ChatGPT, which introduced similar personal finance tools in May that also let users connect their financial accounts and ask questions about everything from spending patterns to long-term financial planning.
“Claude gives you answers in everyday language, from your balances and transactions, and explains any term that’s new to you,” Anthropic wrote in a blog post. “Like the rest of Claude, Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations, and it doesn’t offer credit cards, loans, or savings accounts of its own, so your money questions get a straight answer.”
For instance, at the end of the month, a user could ask Claude, “Where did my money go this month?” The chatbot will then add up spending across the connected accounts and sort it by category, such as rent and utilities, food and drink, and shopping. Users can choose to go deeper by following up with questions like, “Is that more than usual?” or “Anything else I’m missing?”
Anthropic says the tool goes beyond basic spending summaries by analyzing transactions across connected accounts to flag potential issues, such as duplicate charges, unexpected fees, and steadily increasing bills. Users can also ask broader questions about their finances, such as whether they’re spending more than they earn. The tool can also explain financial concepts like APR (annual percentage rate), while providing calculations that show users how much they’ve paid in interest over the past year.
Of course, some people will have reservations about connecting their financial accounts to an AI chatbot. Anthropic says Claude’s access is limited to each connected bank’s name, account name and type, the last four digits of the account number, balances, credit limits, and up to two years of transaction history.
Additionally, the company notes that when users chat with Claude in the Personal Finance hub, those conversations aren’t used to train its models.
Personal Finance starts rolling out in beta this week to users on the Pro, Max, and Ultra plans in the U.S.
The launch of the new tool comes as Anthropic has been expanding Claude into new verticals. For instance, Anthropic launched Claude for Legal and Claude for Financial Services earlier this year.

Food delivery startup Wonder files for IPO as it explores its next big bite
9:11 AM PST · November 5, 2026
Food delivery startup Wonder is moving closer to becoming a publicly traded company after confidentially filing for an initial public offering (IPO). The company announced the filing on Thursday, marking a major milestone following years of fundraising, acquisitions, and expansion.
Wonder has yet to reveal how many shares it plans to make available or the expected price range.
Founded in 2018 by entrepreneur Marc Lore, Wonder has evolved from a food delivery concept into a broader food technology business. Its model goes beyond traditional delivery apps, with the company operating food hall-style locations where customers can order meals from multiple restaurant brands through a single platform. The company handles everything from meal preparation to delivery, pickup, and dine-in service.
Lore, who previously founded Jet.com and Diapers.com, has made no secret of his plans to take Wonder public. Those ambitions gained further attention in July, when the company announced it had raised more than $650 million in a funding round that valued it at around $9 billion. Investors include Accel, GV, AllianceBernstein, and ARK Invest.
Meanwhile, Wonder has been busy expanding its footprint and strengthening its business through acquisitions. The company has outlined ambitious growth plans, including a major push into Texas, where it aims to open more than 100 locations by the end of 2027.
Additionally, Wonder has acquired meal-kit company Blue Apron, restaurant delivery platform Grubhub, media company Tastemade, and kitchen robotics company Spyce. The latter acquisition gives Wonder access to automation technology that could help streamline food preparation and improve how food is served.
Wonder is also branching out with Wonder Create, its platform focused on letting food entrepreneurs and social media influencers develop new food concepts, restaurant brands, and menu items. The platform leverages AI to design and launch restaurant brands in less than a minute.
Another notable move is its $425 million partnership with DoorDash to expand its campus dining business, which operates at 450 colleges and universities and other locations.
Despite its growth, a move into the public markets will bring new challenges. Wonder is operating in an increasingly competitive food delivery landscape, going up against established names such as DoorDash and Uber Eats.

Bluesky hit peak usage for the year on election night
The blue wave swept Bluesky on Tuesday night as the microblogging platform recorded its highest daily number of posts, replies, and likes in 2026.
“We’re seeing a wave of new people joining and old friends coming back,” Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider posted.
According to Schneider, posts and likes doubled during the U.S. midterm elections on Tuesday.
COO Rose Wang told TechCrunch that usage began to peak between 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. PT, when many election results were rolling in. Daily posts and likes increased 30% and 70%, respectively, compared to the previous 30-day averages; clicks on links also spiked 20%.
are we about to break the all-time record for likes in a single day??
— alex benzer (@alexbenzer.com) 2026-11-05T00:24:42.561Z
According to open source data, Bluesky reached 44 million likes, 4.8 million posts, and 2 million new follows on November 4. This nearly eclipsed Bluesky’s all-time record 45 million likes in a single day, set in November 2024.
This jump was especially visible in Bluesky’s data traffic, which was 200% higher than usual, reaching up to 35.8 GB/s.
Bluesky is — sometimes snidely — referred to as “Twitter for the left,” given that its user base seems to skew that way politically. This isn’t a coincidence; Bluesky’s most concentrated period of user growth occurred after Donald Trump won the 2024 presidential election, so it makes sense that those users would post actively during a night of overwhelming victories for the Democratic party.

Dropbox acquires Tigris Data for $350M to bolster its AI infrastructure
7:19 AM PST · November 5, 2026
Dropbox is making a big push into AI infrastructure with a $350 million acquisition of cloud technology company Tigris Data, marking what appears to be its largest acquisition to date.
Announced Thursday, the deal is expected to strengthen Dropbox’s AI infrastructure capabilities and support the development of DBX Agent Cloud, a new storage platform aimed at businesses and developers building AI models and agents.
Dropbox told TechCrunch via email that the transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. The company also said it currently has no plans to reduce headcount as part of the acquisition. The company already cut 9% of its global workforce last month, WSJ reported.
DBX Agent Cloud will initially offer object storage as a stand-alone product, allowing businesses to purchase storage independently and use it with existing tools and applications built for Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service), which is a cloud storage service that enables businesses to store and retrieve large volumes of data.
Beyond its infrastructure ambitions, Dropbox is also bringing more AI capabilities to its core product. Users will be able to ask AI to perform supported tasks using their files, choose between different AI models, and connect their Dropbox content to third-party tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Muse.
The company also plans to expand DBX Agent Cloud with additional capabilities designed to help AI systems work with different types of content, including documents, images, audio, and video. Other planned additions include filesystem features that will allow AI agents to manage files and maintain continuity across tasks and sessions.
Dropbox says the updated experience has already reached more than 70,000 teams. The initial rollout is available to eligible Standard and Advanced customers in the U.S., U.K., and Australia, with broader availability planned for 2027.
Tigris Data was founded by former Uber engineers who helped develop the ride-hailing company’s storage infrastructure. The company provides cloud storage technology that helps businesses store and access data across different regions. Its platform automatically positions data closer to the users and computing resources that need it, helping reduce access times and improve performance.
Tigris Data raised $25 million in a Series A funding round last year.
While the Tigris deal appears to be Dropbox’s largest acquisition, it is not the company’s first move to expand its AI capabilities through M&A. Dropbox has previously acquired several AI-focused companies, including Reclaim.ai, Promoted.ai, and Mobius Labs.

content:
香港保安局局长邓克里斯表示，当局将在本月晚些时候的悲剧周年纪念日向那些希望纪念宏福苑火灾遇难者的人们提供帮助，前提是此类活动“合法”。保安局局长邓克里斯。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。唐在周四的一次活动中向记者发表讲话时发表了上述讲话，距离致命火灾一周年纪念日还有大约三周。去年11月26日，该村大规模翻修工程中发生大火，吞噬了7栋大楼，造成168人死亡、4600多名居民流离失所。 “很多家人和朋友都想纪念这一天，我们完全理解这一点。只要是合法的行动，我们都会尽力提供便利，”唐说。去年火灾发生后，香港人在广福休憩处设立了一个临时守夜地点，该休憩处是遭受火灾破坏的宏福苑附近的一个公园。火灾发生几天后，经过与警方的协调，该处已被清理干净。同样在悲剧发生后，政府发布的一份新闻稿猛烈抨击“反华势力和不稳定势力”“发表毫无根据的诽谤性言论”，并试图借火“煽动社会混乱”。 2025 年 12 月 8 日，志愿者在宏福村附近的休息区为大埔火灾受害者移走鲜花、留言和其他悼念品。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
警察国家安全局总警司李志强在火灾发生后表示，他曾到过大埔现场，他认为“情况越来越像‘黑衣暴力’”，指的是2019年民主示威者所穿的衣服。另见：大埔火灾：警方监督连夜清除鲜花、志愿者和政府工作人员向纪念碑致敬的活动。他指出，“基本上是‘黑衣暴力’的小册子和标语”与灾难无关，只是为了煽动仇恨。”中国政府以及北京负责香港事务的最高办公室继续引用一种说法，指责某些行为者利用这场悲剧作为借口，在火灾发生后的几个月里制造混乱。唐周四表示：“我相信，如果依法处理，我们一定会提供帮助。”唐还重申了政府的部分改革建议，并表示当局将采取多管齐下的方法，包括提出立法修正案和协调执法机构，以防止未来串通投标。

【原文 English Original】
Authorities will assist people wishing to commemorate the victims of the Wang Fuk Court blaze on the tragedy’s anniversary later this month, on the condition that such activities are “lawful,” Hong Kong security chief Chris Tang has said. Secretary for Security Chris Tang. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Tang made the remarks when addressing reporters at an event on Thursday, some three weeks ahead of the first anniversary of the deadly fire. The blaze broke out on November 26 last year, engulfing seven buildings in the subsidised housing estate during large-scale renovation works, killing 168 people and displacing over 4,600 residents. “Many family members and friends want to commemorate this day and we fully understand this. We will do our best to facilitate any actions as long as they are handled lawfully,” Tang said. In the wake of the blaze last year, Hongkongers set up a makeshift vigil site at the Kwong Fuk Sitting-out Area, a park near the fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court. It was cleared out days after the fire following coordination with the police. ‘In accordance with the law’ Also in the wake of the tragedy, a government press release blasted “anti-China and destabilising forces” for “making unfounded and slanderous remarks,” and trying to use the fire to “stir up chaos in society.” Volunteers remove flowers, messages and other tributes for Tai Po fire victims at a rest area near Wang Fuk Estate on December 8, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Chief Superintendent of the police’s National Security Department Steve Li said after the fire that he had visited the Tai Po site and that he believed “the situation was becoming more and more like that of ‘black-clad violence,'” in reference to clothing worn by 2019 pro-democracy demonstrators. See also: Tai Po fire: Police oversee overnight removal of flowers, tributes from memorial by volunteers, gov’t staff He pointed to pamphlets and slogans that were “basically unrelated to the disaster and only aimed to incite hatred.” The government — and Beijing’s top office on Hong Kong affairs — has continued to reference a narrative accusing certain actors of using the tragedy as a pretence for sowing chaos in the months since the fire. Tang said on Thursday: “I believe that if they are handled in accordance with the law, we will certainly assist.” Tang also reiterated part of the government’s reform proposals, saying that the authorities would adopt a multi-pronged approach including introducing legislative amendments and coordinating law enforcement agencies to prevent bid-rigging in the future.

title: ‘6 years in jail has reshaped my view of life’: Joshua Wong sought leniency to be freed in his 30s, mitigation letter reveals
zh_title: “六年监禁重塑了我的人生观”：缓刑信显示黄之锋在30多岁时寻求宽大处理以获释
summary: 被监禁的香港活动人士黄之锋在周四宣判前向法庭提交的一份缓刑信中表示，六年的监禁重塑了他的人生观，要求给予最大程度的宽大处理，以便他能够在三十多岁的时候重获自由。 2019 年 9 月 28 日，民主活动人士黄之锋宣布参加香港 2019 年区议会选举。照片：Philip Fong/法新社。周四，高等法院法官谭威廉 (William Tam) 判处这名活动人士 10 年监禁，此前，黄承认串谋与外国势力共谋，这是他根据 Be 法案第二次被定罪。
content:
被监禁的香港活动人士黄之锋在周四宣判前向法庭提交的一份缓刑信中表示，六年的监禁重塑了他的人生观，要求给予最大程度的宽大处理，以便他能够在三十多岁的时候重获自由。 2019 年 9 月 28 日，民主活动人士黄之锋宣布参加香港 2019 年区议会选举。照片：Philip Fong/法新社。周四，高等法院法官谭威廉判处这名活动人士 10 年监禁，此前黄先生承认了串谋外国势力的罪名，这是他根据北京实施的国家安全法第二次被定罪。这位30岁的男子自2020年底（当时24岁）以来一直入狱。他因在具有里程碑意义的“香港47”案中串谋颠覆国家政权而被判入狱四年零八个月，原定于2027年初获释，但去年6月被指控犯有与外国勾结的罪名。在 HKFP 获得的一封中文缓解信中，黄说他错过了大学毕业典礼，并失去了与家人在一起的 2000 多天。 “与90年代出生的同龄人不同，我无法组建自己的家庭，也无法进入职场。相反，我只能在简陋的牢房里看着岁月流逝，”信中写道。黄说，在监狱期间，他每天定期锻炼身体、读书、学习新技能。
他补充说，他正在学习吉他，准备国际英语语言测试系统（雅思），并参加了当地大学举办的多门法律和商业课程。黄在信中说：“我向法官大人保证，我不会让自己被24岁之前的自己所定义……当我走出这个牢房的那一天，我祈祷我能洗掉24岁的天真，以成熟的思想、丰富的知识和健康的身体向前迈进。” 2026 年 11 月 5 日黄之锋被判刑后，领事馆代表在高等法院。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。该活动人士还表示，希望出狱后能够照顾年迈的父母并回馈社会。 “我因《国安法》入狱的经历并没有让我拒绝对中国有更深入的了解。相反，它促使我博览群书，汲古思今……我希望运用自己的专业技能，在完全依法的情况下为社会经济发展做出贡献。” “势不可挡”的情况黄被指控与自我流亡的活动人士罗冠聪和其他未透露姓名的人士合谋，在北京实施的国家安全法于2020年6月生效后，要求外国对香港和中国大陆政府实施制裁和封锁，或从事其他敌对活动。
在2019年的抗议和骚乱期间，许多抗议者在国际上开展活动，争取西方国家的支持，并向香港和北京当局施压，以满足他们的要求。黄在他的缓和信中表示，国家安全法生效后，他意识到呼吁外国制裁是非法的，他“立即停止了所有此类言论和行为”。黄之锋在7月1日身穿众志T恤。照片：众志，来自 Facebook。 “然而，随着法律的突然生效，情况变得不堪重负。我在困惑中试图调整自己的言行，但我的法律判断

【原文 English Original】
Jailed Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong has said in a mitigation letter submitted to court before his sentencing on Thursday that his six years in prison reshaped his outlook on life, asking for the utmost leniency so he could walk free in his thirties. Pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong announcing his run for the 2019 District Council elections in Hong Kong on September 28, 2019. Photo: Philip Fong/AFP. High Court judge William Tam sentenced the activist to 10 years’ imprisonment on Thursday after Wong pleaded guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces, his second conviction under a Beijing-imposed national security law. The 30-year-old has been behind bars since late 2020, when he was 24. He was due to be released in early 2027 after completing a four-year, eight-month jail term for conspiracy to subvert state power in the landmark “Hong Kong 47” case, but was charged with foreign collusion in June last year. In a Chinese-language mitigation letter obtained by HKFP, Wong said he had missed his university graduation ceremony and lost more than 2,000 days with his family. “Unlike my peers born in the 1990s, I was unable to start a family of my own or enter the workforce. Instead, I could only watch the years pass inside a stark cell,” the letter reads. Wong said that while in prison, he exercised regularly, read books, and learned new skills every day. He added that he was learning the guitar, preparing for the International English Language Testing System (IELTS), and taking multiple legal and business courses organised by local universities. “I pledge to Your Honour that I will not allow myself to be defined by who I was before the age of 24… When the day comes that I step out of this cell, I pray that I will have washed away the naivety of 24, moving forward with a mature mind, enriched knowledge, and a healthy body,” Wong said in the letter. Consulate representatives at the High Court after Joshua Wong’s sentencing on November 5, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The activist also said he hoped to care for his elderly parents and give back to society upon his release. “My experience of imprisonment under the National Security Law has not made me resistant to gaining a deeper understanding of China. On the contrary, it drove me to read extensively, draw wisdom from the past to reflect on the present… I hope to apply my professional skills to contribute to the socio-economic development of our society in full compliance with the law.” ‘Overwhelming’ situation Wong was accused of conspiring with self-exiled activist Nathan Law and other unnamed individuals after the Beijing-imposed national security law came into effect in June 2020 to request that foreign countries impose sanctions and blockades, or engage in other hostile activities, directed against the governments of Hong Kong and mainland China. During the 2019 protests and unrest, many protesters campaigned internationally to gather support from Western countries and pressure Hong Kong and Beijing authorities to meet their demands. Wong said in his mitigation letter that once the national security law came into effect, he realised that calling for foreign sanctions was unlawful and he “promptly ceased all such statements and conduct.” Joshua Wong in July 1 march wearing a T-shirt of Demosisto. Photo: Demosisto, via Facebook. “However, as the law suddenly came into force, the situation was overwhelming. I attempted to adjust my words and actions amid confusion, yet my legal judgment was not thorough and I was not in a clear mind, leaving me unable to properly determine the legal boundaries for every single act,” Wong said. “At the time, I believed that reposting publications by others, or urging foreign enterprises on commercial grounds to halt cooperation with police, differed from directly calling for sanctions,” he said, adding: “With respect to all statements I made and posts I published, I admit them in their entirety and accept full responsibility.” Protests erupted in June 2019 over a since-axed extradition bill . They escalated into sometimes violent displays of dissent against police behaviour, amid calls for democracy and anger over Beijing’s encroachment. Demonstrators demanded an independent probe into police conduct, amnesty for those arrested and a halt to the characterisation of protests as “riots.”

title: Au Kam San: The teacher-turned-lawmaker who called ‘bluntly’ for democracy in Macau
zh_title: 区锦新：“直言不讳”呼吁澳门民主的教师出身的议员
summary: 前澳门立法会议员区锦新曾是中国赌场中心争取民主的领军人物，但在周五被判犯有“颠覆国家政权”罪后，他将在接下来的十年里在监狱里度过。这张照片拍摄于 2024 年 12 月 12 日，小学教师区锦新 (Au Kam-san) 成为澳门任职时间最长的民主派立法会议员之一，他在澳门摆姿势拍照。照片：爱德华多·莱尔/法新社。区被判处12年零6个月监禁，还被指控“与外部团体和个人建立联系”和“违反保密规定”。他的审判是第一次
content:
前澳门立法会议员区锦新曾是中国赌场中心争取民主的领军人物，但在周五被判犯有“颠覆国家政权”罪后，他将在接下来的十年里在监狱里度过。这张照片拍摄于 2024 年 12 月 12 日，小学教师区锦新 (Au Kam-san) 成为澳门任职时间最长的民主派立法会议员之一，他在澳门摆姿势拍照。照片：爱德华多·莱尔/法新社。区被判处12年零6个月监禁，还被指控“与外部团体和个人建立联系”和“违反保密规定”。对他的审判是这个前葡萄牙殖民地根据《国家安全法》审理的第一起案件。该法于 2009 年颁布，并于 2023 年加强。对欧的审判是闭门进行的，观察人士称，这在该市是史无前例的，听证会只花了三天时间。区议员的老师最初将教学视为自己一生的工作，但在 1989 年北京天安门广场镇压后，他转向从政，认为澳门应该变得开放和民主。几十年来，他帮助组织了每年一度的守夜活动，以纪念天安门事件的受害者。区先生的政治生涯始于1993年，当时他当选为市议员。欧金山.照片：Au Kam San，来自 Facebook。 2001年至2021年间，他五次当选澳门立法会议员，是小型民主派阵营中任职时间最长的立法会议员之一。
“作为一名土生土长的澳门居民，我在日常生活中看到了社会上的许多问题，非常需要有人站出来，让当局承担责任，”欧在 2013 年的一个电视节目中说道。 前激进主义盟友 Jason Chao 告诉法新社，在澳门，欧被视为“敢于对抗当权者”。据赵说，他在 2000 年代揭露了多起涉及官员的腐败丑闻。在前同事眼中，欧有两种截然相反的一面：他会在立法机关发起猛烈批评，但会在街头温和劝说，鼓励公众参政。澳门和中国政治专家Eilo Yu表示，区先生被视为“说话相当直率”的人。公民空间萎缩2019年，中国金融中心香港发生了规模巨大、有时甚至是暴力的抗议活动，随之而来的镇压也让邻近的澳门的政治气氛降温。欧在 2021 年表示，他不会竞选连任，但表示会留在澳门。那一年，澳门当局禁止了欧与共同组织的天安门守夜活动，称该活动将“煽动颠覆”。中国赌场中心后来于 2023 年扩大了国家安全法的范围，官员称这是为了防止外国干涉。澳门立法会大楼。照片：澳门政府欧承认澳门在民主方面几乎没有取得什么进展，但表示他相信“播下种子并给它们成长的机会”。
欧在2024年对法新社表示：“尽管我们正处于严冬，但如果外部环境发生变化，澳门的这些种子可能仍有机会发芽，开辟一条通向民主的新道路。”他在立法会任期结束后继续就政治和社会问题发表讲话。 2025 年 7 月被捕前几天，区谴责澳门的国家安全法“推翻了无罪推定原则”，以回应当局取消一些选举候选人的资格。 Au当时在社交媒体上写道：“讽刺的是，正是那些被定义为‘un

【原文 English Original】
Former Macau lawmaker Au Kam San was once a leading figure in the Chinese casino hub’s fight for democracy, but will spend the next decade behind bars after he was found guilty on Friday of “subversion”. This photo taken on December 12, 2024 shows Au Kam-san, a primary school teacher who became one of Macau’s longest-serving pro-democracy legislators, posing for a portrait in Macau. Photo: Eduardo Leal/AFP. Au, who was sentenced to 12 years and six months in jail , was also accused of “building links with external groups and individuals” and “breaching confidentiality”. His trial is the first case under the National Security Law in the former Portuguese colony, which was enacted in 2009 and toughened in 2023. Au was tried behind closed doors, which observers say was unprecedented in the city, and hearings took only three days. Teacher to legislator Au initially saw teaching as his life’s work, but he switched to politics following the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown in Beijing, believing that Macau should become open and democratic. For decades, he helped to organise annual vigils to commemorate the victims of Tiananmen. Au’s political career began in 1993 when he was elected as a municipal councillor. Au Kam San. Photo: Au Kam San, via Facebook. Between 2001 and 2021, he was elected to Macau’s legislature five times and was one of the longest-serving lawmakers from the small pro-democracy camp. “As a native Macau resident, I see many problems in society in my daily life, and there is a great need for someone to stand up and hold the authorities to account,” Au told a television programme in 2013. Jason Chao, a former activist ally, told AFP that Au was viewed in Macau as being “unafraid to stand up to those in power”. He uncovered several corruption scandals involving officials during the 2000s, according to Chao. In the eyes of former colleagues, Au had two contrasting sides: he would launch fierce criticisms in the legislature, but use gentle persuasion on the streets to encourage public participation in politics. Eilo Yu, an expert in Macau and China politics, said Au was seen as someone who “speaks rather bluntly”. Shrinking civic space In 2019, the Chinese finance hub of Hong Kong saw huge and sometimes violent protests, and the ensuing crackdown also chilled the political climate in neighbouring Macau. Au said in 2021 that he would not run for re-election, though he said he would stay in Macau. That year, Macau authorities banned the Tiananmen vigil co-organised by Au, saying the event would “incite subversion”. The Chinese casino hub later expanded the scope of its national security laws in 2023, which officials said was to prevent foreign interference. Macau’s Legislative Assembly building. Photo: MacauGov. Au conceded that Macau had made little progress toward democracy, but said he believed in “sowing seeds and giving them a chance to grow”. “Even though we are in a bitter winter, if there are changes to the external environment, these seeds in Macau may yet have a chance to sprout and forge a new path towards democracy,” Au told AFP in 2024. He continued to speak out on political and social issues after his term as lawmaker ended. Days before his arrest in July 2025, Au condemned Macau’s national security law for “overturning the principle of the presumption of innocence”, in response to authorities disqualifying some election candidates. Au wrote on social media at the time: “Ironically, it is precisely those defined as ‘unpatriotic’ who are the ones most capable of criticising social ills, speaking out most boldly and advocating most vigorously for the people, whether in the legislature or in society at large.”

title: Police say linking mall cameras to AI facial recognition network complies with Hong Kong privacy laws
zh_title: 警方表示，将商场摄像头连接到人工智能面部识别网络符合香港隐私法
summary: 警方表示，为香港的闭路电视网络配备人工智能面部识别软件并将其连接到购物中心的安全摄像头不会违反当地的隐私法。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。据当地媒体周五报道，警方表示，人工智能面部识别功能最早将于本月添加到该市的 SmartView 监控系统中，今年将有四家私人购物中心连接到该网络。据了解，这四间商场分别为大角咀奥海城、屯门市广场、葵涌商场及四二商场
content:
警方表示，为香港的闭路电视网络配备人工智能面部识别软件并将其连接到购物中心的安全摄像头不会违反当地的隐私法。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。据当地媒体周五报道，警方表示，人工智能面部识别功能最早将于本月添加到该市的 SmartView 监控系统中，今年将有四家私人购物中心连接到该网络。据当地媒体报道，这四家商场分别是大角咀的奥海城、屯门市广场、葵涌商场和粉岭的Sierra Life。警方行动科高级警司梁明亮表示，人工智能面部识别系统不会全天候运行，而是需要督察或以上级别的警官批准。 “我们首先要问的是，使用SmartView对于破案是否至关重要。必须审查多少个摄像头和多少镜头？这个范围是否符合调查目标？在批准任何申请之前，必须解决这些问题，”梁用粤语说。他表示，该技术将通过自动识别嫌疑人或失踪人员的面部是否在特定时间范围内的特定区域被摄像机捕捉到，帮助警察追查嫌疑人或失踪人员。梁补充说，或者，该系统可以实时追踪一个人的脸部，提醒警察他们出现的时间和地点。
闭路电视录像将在捕获后30天自动删除，而时间戳和位置等元数据将保留长达180天。“额外好处”梁还表示，根据警方法律团队和个人资料私隐专员的评估，与购物中心的连接不会违反隐私法。旺角的闭路电视摄像机。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 “这些商场已经配备了安全摄像头，通常与我们的 SmartView 系统具有相同的公共安全目的。连接到它们只是一个额外的好处，”他说。 SmartView项目于2024年启动，截至上个月，已帮助破获2,000起犯罪案件，并逮捕了约2,800名涉嫌谋杀和纵火等罪名的嫌疑人。当局的目标是到 2028 年，通过安装新摄像头并将私人系统和其他政府部门运营的系统连接到警察网络，将全市 60,000 个监控摄像头纳入该系统。 SmartView 第三阶段计划在 2028 年至 2031 年间再安装 6,500 个监控摄像头。

【原文 English Original】
Equipping Hong Kong’s CCTV network with AI facial recognition software and connecting it to shopping mall security cameras would not breach local privacy laws, police have said. A CCTV camera in Mong Kok. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Police have said that the AI facial recognition feature will be added to the city’s SmartView surveillance system as early as this month, with four private shopping malls set to be connected to the network this year, local media reported on Friday. The four malls are understood to be Olympian City in Tai Kok Tsui, Tuen Mun Town Plaza, Kwai Chung Shopping Centre, and Sierra Life in Fanling, local media reported . Leung Ming-leung, a senior superintendent in the police’s Operations Bureau, said the AI facial recognition system would not operate round-the-clock, but would instead require sign-off from an officer ranked inspector or above. “We first ask whether using SmartView is essential to solving the crime. How many cameras and how much footage must be reviewed? Does that scope align with the investigation’s objectives? These points must be settled before any application is approved,” Leung said in Cantonese. He said the technology would help officers track down suspects or missing persons by automatically identifying whether their faces had been caught on camera in a particular area during a specific timeframe. Alternatively, the system could trace an individual’s face in real time, alerting officers to when and where they appear, Leung added. The CCTV footage will be automatically deleted 30 days after capture, while metadata such as timestamps and locations will be retained for up to 180 days. ‘Added bonus’ Leung also said that the connections to shopping malls would not breach privacy laws, based on assessments by the police’s legal team and the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data. A CCTV camera in Mong Kok. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “These malls are already equipped with security cameras, often serving the same public safety purpose as our SmartView system. Linking into them is merely an added bonus,” he said. The SmartView project was launched in 2024 and, as of last month, had helped solve 2,000 crimes and led to the arrest of about 2,800 suspects on charges including murder and arson. Authorities aim to incorporate 60,000 surveillance cameras across the city into the system by 2028, by installing new cameras and linking private systems and those operated by other government departments to the police network. A further 6,500 surveillance cameras are planned between 2028 and 2031 under SmartView’s third phase.

title: Hong Kong national security police arrest man over allegedly importing ‘seditious’ books
zh_title: 香港国安警察逮捕涉嫌进口“煽动性”书籍的男子
summary: 香港国安警察在今年早些时候打击独立书店后的最新执法行动中逮捕了一名涉嫌进口“煽动性书籍”的男子。香港警队徽章。照片：Candice Chau/HKFP。警方周四在一份声明中表示，他们在旺角逮捕了一名 34 岁男子。他涉嫌“进口具有煽动意图的出版物”——触犯《维护国家安全条例》（又称《维护国家安全条例》第23条）。被捕者据悉是“等待鸟”项目经理布兰登·丘（Brandon Yau）
content:
香港国安警察在今年早些时候打击独立书店后的最新执法行动中逮捕了一名涉嫌进口“煽动性书籍”的男子。香港警队徽章。照片：Candice Chau/HKFP。警方周四在一份声明中表示，他们在旺角逮捕了一名 34 岁男子。他涉嫌“进口具有煽动意图的出版物”，这是《维护国家安全条例》（又称《维护国家安全条例》第23条）规定的犯罪行为。据了解，被捕者是“等待鸟”组织的项目经理布兰登·丘（Brandon Yau），该组织为因政治相关案件而入狱的人提供支持。这些书籍被进口并在其合作伙伴零售店 As One 销售，其收入归该集团所有。周一，Waiting Bird 在社交媒体上发帖称，海关从一批来自台湾的货物中查获了约 60 本书。该组织表示，没收的书籍是“对时事、个人经历和感受的理性讨论，与煽动意图没有任何关系”。警方在声明中表示，被捕者是一名公司董事，“涉嫌向当地书店进口煽动性书籍，意图向香港和中国政府带来仇恨、蔑视或不满”。作为爱德华王子中的一员。照片：Nidou Workspace，来自 Google 地图。
警方还搜查了该男子的住所和公司场所，查获了包括用于购买书籍的数字设备在内的物品，以及涉嫌具有煽动意图的文件和其他出版物。该男子已被拘留接受调查。进口具有煽动意图的出版物最高可判处七年监禁。香港当局今年加强了对独立书店的审查。书店老板表示，从台湾（许多中文书籍的来源地）订购的书籍经常受到海关检查。 Book Punch 的工作人员于 3 月份被捕，Hunter 书店的工作人员于 6 月份被捕。 7月，Have a Nice Stay和Greenfield书店的工作人员在同一天被捕。逮捕前一天，Have a Nice Stay 宣布将在运营四年后关闭。逮捕事件发生后，格林菲尔德书店还表示，明年租约到期后将关闭。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong national security police have arrested a man over allegedly importing “seditious books” in the latest law enforcement action following a crackdown on independent bookstores earlier this year. The Hong Kong Police Force emblem. Photo: Candice Chau/HKFP. Police said in a statement on Thursday that they had arrested a 34-year-old man in Mong Kok. He was suspected of “importing a publication that has a seditious intention” – a crime under the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, also known as Article 23. The arrestee is understood to be Brandon Yau, a project manager at Waiting Bird, a group that supports people jailed in politics-related cases. The books were imported to be sold at As One, its partner retail outlet whose revenue goes towards the group. On Monday, Waiting Bird said in a social media post that Customs had seized around 60 books from a shipment that came from Taiwan. The group said the books confiscated were “rational discussions about current affairs, and personal experiences and feelings, with no connection whatsoever to seditious intentions.” In the statement, police said the person arrested was a company director “suspected of importing seditious books into local bookstores with the intent to bring hatred, contempt or disaffection” to the Hong Kong and Chinese governments. As One in Prince Edward. Photo: Nidou Workspace, via Google Maps. Officers also searched the man’s residence and company premises, seizing items including digital devices used to purchase the books, as well as documents and other publications suspected of having seditious intention. The man has been detained for investigation. Importing a publication with seditious intention carries a maximum sentence of seven years in jail. Hong Kong authorities have tightened scrutiny of independent bookstores this year. Bookstore owners have said that books ordered from Taiwan – the source for many Chinese-language titles – are frequently inspected by Customs. Staff from Book Punch were arrested in March, and staff from Hunter Bookstore were apprehended in June. In July, staff from Have a Nice Stay and Greenfield Bookstore were arrested on the same day. A day before the arrests, Have a Nice Stay announced it would close down after four years in operation. Following the arrests, Greenfield Bookstore also said it would shut after its lease expired next year.

title: Macau sentences ex-lawmaker to 12.5 years in first national security trial
zh_title: 澳门首次国家安全审判判处前立法会议员12.5年徒刑
summary: 周五，中国领土澳门一家法院以颠覆国家政权罪和其他罪名，判处前立法会议员、民主运动人士欧锦新 12 年零 6 个月监禁。前澳门议员区锦新。资料图：区金山，来自 Facebook。 69 岁的区先生是澳门第一个因 2023 年扩大的国家安全法而被定罪的人。澳门是前葡萄牙殖民地和赌场中心，于 1999 年回归中国。他与他人共同组织了一年一度的守夜活动，纪念 1989 年北京天安门广场镇压的受害者，此前只有澳门和邻近的香港才容忍这种行为。 Au，被拘留于 J
content:
周五，中国领土澳门一家法院以颠覆国家政权罪和其他罪名，判处前立法会议员、民主运动人士欧锦新 12 年零 6 个月监禁。前澳门议员区锦新。资料图：区金山，来自 Facebook。 69 岁的区先生是澳门第一个因 2023 年扩大的国家安全法而被定罪的人。澳门是前葡萄牙殖民地和赌场中心，于 1999 年回归中国。他与他人共同组织了一年一度的守夜活动，纪念 1989 年北京天安门广场镇压的受害者，此前只有澳门和邻近的香港才容忍这种行为。法院声明称，区于 2025 年 7 月被拘留，9 月闭门审判在三天内结束，被判犯有“颠覆国家政治权力”等罪名。报告称，区帮助“外部敌对组织收集、准备和公开传播各种明显充满颠覆性政治主张、反对国家政治权威的图像和信息”。声明补充说，他还试图“煽动澳门居民对中国的仇恨”，意图“推翻和破坏中国宪法规定的国家基本制度”。
澳门政府对判决表示欢迎，并誓言“严格执行澳门国家安全法，防范、制止和惩治危害国家安全的行为”。声明补充说，将“确保澳门特色‘一国两制’原则长期稳定实施”。欧盟去年谴责了他的逮捕，称这只会加剧人们对澳门“政治多元化受到侵蚀”的担忧。2026 年 11 月 6 日，澳门初审法院外看到一辆囚车。照片：Tommy Wang/法新社。 “海外正义”组织在 7 月份的一份声明中表示，自 Au 被拘留后不久起，他的家人就不允许与他见面或交谈。声明援引他女儿 Cherry 的话说：“我父亲将自己 30 多年的一生奉献给了澳门人民。” “快一年过去了，我们仍然无法与他取得联系。” “假审判” 海外司法部主任、伦敦大律师迈克尔·波拉克(Michael Polak)表示，他担任区的国际律师，他周五表示，对这位葡萄牙公民的“假审判”“给澳门带来了耻辱”。波拉克在另一份声明中表示，他的命运“使澳门与世界上最专制的国家保持一致，这些国家的行政部门有权监禁那些与其意见不同的人，而没有任何适当、公平的法律程序。”法院周五表示，已批准区家人探访监狱。
“从闭门审判到公开宣判，这是一个什么样的过程？这是一次政治审判，”欧的妻子弗吉尼亚·郑妙珊(Virginia Cheang Mio San)周五在一封公开信中写道。 “这是毫无根据的迫害，践踏人的尊严！”她写道。只有少数当地媒体获准进入法庭，官员们指责座位有限。前澳门议员区锦新。资料图：区金山，来自 Facebook。欧是一名教师，但在 1989 年中国镇压之后，他开始相信澳门迫切需要成为一个开放、民主的社会，并进入政坛。 “我承认，在争取民主的斗争中，我们一无所获，但我相信播下种子并给它们成长的机会，”他于 202 年告诉法新社

【原文 English Original】
A court in Chinese territory Macau sentenced ex-lawmaker and democracy campaigner Au Kam San to 12 years and six months in prison on Friday for subversion and other offences. Former Macau lawmaker Au Kam San. File photo: Au Kam San, via Facebook. Au, 69, is the first person convicted under national security laws widened in 2023 in Macau, the former Portuguese colony and casino hub which reverted to China in 1999. He co-organised annual vigils for victims of the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown in Beijing, something previously tolerated only in Macau and neighbouring Hong Kong. Au, detained in July 2025 and whose closed-door trial concluded in September within three days, was found guilty of “subversion against the political power of the State” among other offences, a court statement said. Au helped “external hostile organisations in the collection, preparation, and public dissemination of various images and information that were manifestly filled with political claims of a subversive nature against the political authority of the State,” it said. He also sought to “incite hatred among Macau residents” against China, with the intent to “overthrow and undermine the fundamental system” of the state enshrined in the Chinese constitution, it added. Macao’s government welcomed the verdict, vowing to “strictly enforce the Macao National Security Law, prevent, stop, and punish acts endangering national security.” It added in a statement that it would “ensure the steady and long-term implementation of the ‘One Country, Two Systems’ principle with Macao characteristics.” The European Union condemned his arrest last year, saying it only heightened concerns about the “erosion of political pluralism” in Macau. A prison van is seen outside the Court of First Instance in Macau on November 6, 2026. Photo: Tommy Wang/AFP. The organisation Justice Abroad said in a statement in July that Au’s family had not been permitted to see or speak to him since shortly after he was detained. “My father dedicated more than 30 years of his life to serving the people of Macau,” his daughter Cherry was quoted as saying in the statement. “Nearly a year has passed, and we are still unable to communicate with him.” ‘Sham trial’ Michael Polak, director of Justice Abroad and a London barrister who said he acts as Au’s international counsel, said on Friday that the “sham trial” of the Portuguese citizen “brings shame upon Macao”. His fate “brings Macao in line with the most repressive states around the world, where the executive has the power to imprison those with whom it disagrees, with no semblance of a proper, fair legal process,” Polak said in a separate statement. The court said on Friday that it has approved prison visits for Au’s family. “From a closed-door trial to a public sentencing, what kind of process is that? It is a political trial,” Au’s wife Virginia Cheang Mio San wrote in an open letter on Friday. “It is baseless persecution that tramples on a person’s dignity!” she wrote. Only a handful of local media were admitted into the courtroom, with officials blaming limited seating. Former Macau lawmaker Au Kam San. File photo: Au Kam San, via Facebook. Au was a teacher but after the 1989 crackdown in China, he came to believe that Macau urgently needed to become an open, democratic society, and entered politics. “I admit that in the fight for democracy, we have accomplished nothing, but I believe in sowing seeds and giving them a chance to grow,” he told AFP in 2024. “Even though we are in a bitter winter, if there are changes to the external environment, these seeds in Macau may yet have a chance to sprout and forge a new path towards democracy,” he said. Human Rights Watch’s deputy Asia director Maya Wang said Friday that the “unjust prosecution and harsh sentencing… sends a chilling message to all peaceful critics in the territory.” “The authorities’ silencing of pro-democracy voices in (Macau) reflects the Chinese government’s broader assault on dissent and fundamental freedoms,” Wang said, calling for pressure from Portugal and the European Union. On Thursday, Hong Kong democracy campaigner Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 more years in jail under the territory’s national security law , a decision condemned by the United States and others.

title: 林兆彬：中共真正懼怕的，是鏡子裡那個年輕的自己

content: 追光者  2026-11-5 【Pulse 快評｜ 中共真正懼怕的，是鏡子裡那個年輕的自己 （林兆彬）】 黃之鋒再被判囚十年，究竟中共在懼怕甚麼呢？答案是「學生運動」與「海外遊説」。這個恐懼是來自內在記憶，不少中共早期領導人都是學運出身，也長期「勾結」外國勢力蘇聯，在延安時期又遊說美國支持。中共清楚學生運動的力量，在今日學運領袖臉上，更看到自己年輕時的影子。革命成功之後，革命者最怕的，就是下一個革命者。 1919年五四運動，學生走到天安門，喊出「外爭國權，內除國賊」。那時候，張國燾是北京學聯領袖，周恩來在天津主編《學生聯合會報》、創立「覺悟社」。五四的核心其實是學生對權威的反抗，他們不相信政府，不相信條約，正是這種不信任，催生了後來的中共。 1935年的一二·九運動亦是如此，北平學生遊行反對華北自治。姚依林、黃華、蔣南翔學運領袖，後來都成了黨的高幹。姚依林做到政治局常委，副總理；黃華做到外交部長。甚至是江澤民，1940年代在南京中央大學、上海交大期間也積極參與學運，抗議國民黨政府各種政策。 中共害怕學運，因為它了解學運的核心是質疑體制。五四把矛頭指向北洋政府賣國，一二·九質疑國民黨的不抵抗，1989年批評中共腐敗。再者，學生一旦上街，未必會停在「反貪腐」的口號上。學生問更根本的問題：這個政權憑甚麼統治我們？ 學生有時間，有理想，有組織能力；最重要的是，他們還沒有被利益綁架，還相信「真理」，而中共也清楚「真理」是最危險的武器。 看看政府近年如何對待香港的大學。大約從2020年開始，它就不斷強化對大學的控制：校長言行越來越似黨委書記，學生會被消失。校園裡的言論被監控，社團被審查，連悼念宏福苑大火的活動都要經過批准。 那些在天安門廣場上絕食的學生和2019年參與社運的年輕人，與1919年火燒趙家樓的學生，其實很相似。他們都相信自己代表未來，都相信「國家興亡，匹夫有責」。中共知道這種信念一旦擴散，就會像野火一樣燒穿它辛苦建立的秩序。 ｜海外遊説觸動神經 為何中共對所謂「勾結外國勢力」如此敏感？因為他們深知，決定中國過去百年命運的關鍵正是外國勢力，親身體會過外國勢力怎樣改變中國的歷史進程，對於這種力量防範之嚴密，正是源於對自身崛起歷史的認知。 無論是國民黨還是共產黨，早期都深深烙印著「蘇聯基因」。孫中山向西方求援無果後，提出「聯俄容共」，引進蘇聯的資金、武器和列寧式的政黨組織模式，這才有了後來的黃埔軍校與北伐。而中共更是共產國際一手孵化的產物，是共產國際的中國支部，有些暴動會議都曾在蘇聯駐中國領事館內舉行，紅軍長征期間利用蘇聯科技破解國民黨的電報。 抗日戰爭結束後，美國的態度成為了決定中國命運的關鍵變數。當時的中共，為了打破國民黨的政治壟斷並爭取美國支援，在《新華日報》上發表了大量熱烈歌頌美國民主制度的文章。毛澤東在延安甚至向美國外交官明確表示，中國戰後的出路在於實行「美式民主」。 美國特使馬歇爾帶著政治幻想來到中國，試圖以西方的議會民主模式，強行將勢如水火的國共兩黨拉入「聯合政府」。1946年，國軍在東北戰場將林彪部隊打得節節敗退。馬歇爾為了迫蔣介石回到談判桌，以斷絕美援為威脅，強加「六月停戰令」。這給了中共軍隊寶貴的喘息與重組時機，徹底扭轉了東北戰局。 1948年美國總統大選，蔣介石政府因對民主黨時任總統杜魯門的對華武器禁運極度不滿，將籌碼全數押在共和黨候選人杜威身上。結果，杜魯門爆冷連任。不滿蔣介石政府貪污腐敗的杜魯門隨後發表《中美關係白皮書》，徹底中斷對蔣介石的實質援助。 美國當年在關鍵時刻的掣肘與最終的袖手旁觀，客觀上成為了壓垮國民黨政權的最後一根稻草。中國的命運，就這樣徹底滑向了另一個軌道。 中共怕學運，更怕遊説海外的學運，因為它清楚學運的可能性，它自己就是最好的例子。每當學生上街，中共就看到鏡子裡那個年輕的自己。那個自己已經死了，被權力埋葬了，但鏡子還在。

title: Expanding Taiwan’s Resistance Area Complex by way of Japan and the Philippines

简介 台湾存在战略纵深问题。如果遭到入侵，它没有陆地边界，没有邻国可以撤退，也没有腹地可以争取时间。就台湾而言，在中国登陆后幸存下来的军队和抵抗力量将在地理上受到压缩，并在靠近占领军的地方作战，无处可退。在台湾的情况下，“留守部队”的想法，即那些旨在隐藏、生存并最终在前进的敌人的后方地区行动的部队，即使不是不可能，也是极具挑战性的。该岛的孤立将使得进口武器、医疗用品、外国战士和通讯设备变得困难，即使存在运送这些物品的政治意愿。台湾的地理位置既是抵御入侵的防御资产，也是抵御占领的不利因素。背景信息 在入侵之前规划台湾跨越时空的物理抵抗架构需要创造力。美国的原则在这种情况下提供了丰富的信息，但并不特别适合该岛的独特情况。美国陆军特种部队非常规战争条令，包括野战手册 3-05.201，将“区域综合体”定义为秘密的、分散的设施网络，为抵抗运动提供安全、控制、分散和灵活性，实际上是由抵抗运动本身建立和控制的解放区。
手册建议，该地区综合体应包括安全系统、大本营（这在台湾不太可能，但安全屋是可能且需要的）、通信、后勤、医疗设施、补给库、训练区以及逃生和恢复机制。它将综合体细分为外部和内部安全区，围绕抵抗区指挥部建立，在台湾可能会分散而不是合并。该理论模型假设了连续的、可扩展的地面：抵抗力量可以进入的区域，用于将其外部区域与其内部区域分开，并在到达指挥单元之前吸收压力。台湾可以规划和组织一个内部地带。实际上，它无法建造学说所假设的与它并肩而立的外部世界，因为没有毗邻的领土可以放置它。不幸的是，对于台湾来说，人民是“地理的囚徒”，正如蒂姆·马歇尔的同名著作所暗示的那样。外部安全区有几项工作通常与抵抗组织在同一块土地上进行：组织和发展战士和民事支持基础设施，作为新兵来源，提供第一线的深入安全和警报，并向抵抗组织指挥部提供有关区域内敌方活动的及时、准确的情报。
该区域的成员筛选、选择和训练新的抵抗组织成员，其中最有能力的进入正规武装部队，而与他们并肩建立的文职支援部队则收集情报并向抵抗区域指挥单元提供后勤和心理行动支持。该条令中没有一个假设假设外部区域与其支持的部队隔着开阔的水域。台湾的地理位置迫使我们适应而不是放弃这一概念：志愿者的招募和审查、中国海军通过海峡行动的情报收集，以及对地区指挥单位的后勤和通信支持都发生了变化。这些功能必须在医生允许的距离内执行

【原文 English Original】
Introduction Taiwan has a strategic depth problem. If invaded, it has no land border, no neighboring state to retreat into, and no hinterland to buy time. In the case of Taiwan, military and resistance forces that survive a Chinese landing would be geographically compressed and operating in close proximity to the occupying forces, with nowhere to fall back. The idea of “ stay-behind forces ,” those intended to hide, survive, and eventually operate in the rear area of an advancing enemy, is extremely challenging – if not impossible – in the Taiwan scenario. The island’s isolation would make it difficult to import weapons, medical supplies, foreign fighters, and communications equipment, even where the political will to send them existed. Taiwan’s geography is both a defensive asset against invasion and a liability against occupation. Background Information Planning Taiwan’s physical resistance architecture across time and space, prior to invasion, demands creativity. American doctrine is informative in this case but not particularly well-suited to the island’s one-of-a-kind situation. US Army Special Forces Unconventional Warfare doctrine, including Field Manual 3-05.201 , defines an “area complex” as a clandestine, dispersed network of facilities that gives a resistance movement security, control, dispersion, and flexibility, in effect, a liberated zone built and held by the resistance itself. The manuals recommend that the area complex include a security system, base camps (which will be unlikely in Taiwan, but safehouses will be possible and needed), communications, logistics, medical facilities, supply caches, training areas, and escape and recovery mechanisms. It subdivides the complex into an outer and an inner security zone, built around the resistance area command, which would likely be distributed rather than consolidated in Taiwan. The doctrinal model assumes contiguous, expandable ground: territory a resistance force can grow into, use to separate its outer zone from its inner one, and absorb pressure before it reaches command cells. Taiwan can plan and organize an inner zone. Practically, it cannot build the outer one that doctrine assumes sits alongside it, because there is no adjoining territory to put it in. Unfortunately for Taiwan, the people are “prisoners of geography,” as Tim Marshall’s book of the same name suggests. The outer security zone has several jobs that normally happen on the same landmass as the resistance itself: organizing and developing fighters and civilian support infrastructure, serving as a source of recruits, providing the first line of in-depth security and warning, and feeding the resistance area command cells with timely, accurate intelligence on enemy activity within the zone. Members in that zone screen, select, and train new resistance members, with the most capable moving into the regular armed element, while the civilian support element, built alongside them, gathers intelligence and delivers logistical and psychological operations support to resistance area command cells. None of that doctrine assumes the outer zone sits across open water from the force it supports. Taiwan’s geography forces an adaptation rather than an abandonment of the concept: recruitment and vetting of volunteers, intelligence collection on Chinese naval movements through the straits, and logistics and communications support to area command cells all shift. These functions must be performed at a distance that the doctrine never anticipated. Miyako Strait (Image Credit: The Straits Times) Japan and the Philippines Japan and the Philippines are where the missing outer zone of the area complex can go. In fact, they may be the only realistic locations immediately adjacent to Taiwan that can perform that function. While Guam, Palau, Okinawa, and other places may play a role, the requirement here is to develop locations that can serve as immediate, geographically close extensions of the resistance area complex. Yonaguni Island (Image Credit: South China Morning Post) Both countries are already part of the conversation about a Taiwan contingency, and both have said so in their own words rather than having the role assigned to them by outsiders. Sanae Takaichi, Japan’s Prime Minister, told Japan’s parliament on November 7, 2025, that China’s use of armed force against Taiwan could constitute what Japanese law calls a “survival-threatening situation,” the threshold that permits Japan to exercise collective self-defense. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said in August 2025 that a war over Taiwan would draw the Philippines into the conflict regardless of its own preferences, citing proximity and the roughly 180,000 Filipinos residing on the island, and that hope is not a plan. To be clear, neither statement commits either government to a specific military role. The Bashi Channel and Batanes Islands (Image Credit: Robert Luster, StongerNavy.org) Just as geography limits maneuver depth on the island itself, it also narrows where the expanded area complex, depth-by-proxy, could realistically land. Japan’s southwestern Sakishima Islands, particularly Yonaguni, sit 110 kilometers from Taiwan and overlook the Miyako Strait, one of the two principal maritime corridors through which the PLA Navy would seek access to the Western Pacific during a Taiwan conflict. The Philippines’ Batanes Islands sit across the Bashi Channel from Taiwan’s Orchid Island, the second passage , which is 80 kilometers wide . Note that Osumi Strait and Tokara Gap are also available for limited traffic, but for Taiwan operations, the Miyako Strait and Bashi Channel are by far the two principal deep-water exits. Japan is already fortifying Yonaguni with missiles and sensors, while the Philippines has rehearsed rapid anti-ship missile deployments to Batanes during joint exercises with the United States. In addition to the geography requirements of the area complex equation, what is also missing is a special operations mission that’s built to move people, equipment, and information through those same two islands into an occupied Taiwan, and to keep moving them for the resistance once a blockade is in place. Such a mission could include at least four functions. The Resistance Mission The first is communications relay. China has already shown a willingness to sever Taiwan’s connectivity through means short of war: a Chinese-owned vessel was accused of cutting a fiber-optic cable near Keelung Harbor in January 2025, following earlier damage to cables serving Taiwan’s Matsu Islands in 2023. In an actual invasion, isolating Taiwan from the outside world would be an early objective. Relay infrastructure staged on Yonaguni and Batanes, built and rehearsed in peacetime, could keep resistance networks and civilian authorities in contact with the outside world after primary infrastructure fails. The second is unmanned insertion, extraction, and resupply, which helps address the logistics and supply caches that doctrine expects an area complex to maintain internally. Small unmanned surface vessels and unmanned aerial systems, launched at night from Batanes or the Sakishima Islands and running beneath a blockade line, are within current technical reach. This is a mission-planning, basing, and personnel management problem more than a technology problem. Building local relationships, expertise, and staging sites is a peacetime preparation task that retired Special Forces Colonel Brian Petit argued requires a long-dwell, host-embedded advisory presence. Applied to the area-complex concept proposed in this paper, Petit’s idea of a persistent advisory mission adapted to this paper would include US Special Forces not only in Taiwan, but also on the two islands and other locations that would run the resistance pipeline once Taiwan is cut off. An Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) Penetrates A Chinese Blockade with Ammunition, Medical, and Communication Supplies for The Resistance (Fictional Image. Image Credit: Grok AI) The third is facilitating the introduction of foreign volunteers who want to fight for Taiwan, which supports the doctrinal escape-and-recovery mechanism in reverse: instead of moving evaders out of denied territory, the same tradecraft moves vetted personnel in. Ukraine’s International Legion drew thousands of foreign fighters within weeks of the 2022 Russian invasion, staging through Poland and other neighboring states that were not themselves combatants. Taiwan has no land border and no neighbor that could serve that role by geographic accident. Japan and the Philippines are plausible staging grounds for screening, inserting, and, if necessary, extracting foreign volunteers. A fourth function is kinetic interdiction of Chinese naval forces from Japanese or Philippine soil. This function is more challenging to plan, organize, and train during peacetime because of the obvious political sensitivity. Japan’s “survival-threatening situation” authority and the Philippines’ Mutual Defense Treaty with the United States both provide a legal path to this kind of involvement. But activation would likely occur only once Tokyo or Manila has determined that it is already a party to the conflict and pre-determined thresholds have been crossed. Treating Japan and the Philippines as two more US Special Forces advisory locations alongside Taiwan introduces a harder problem: what sustains a pipeline like this over the years is whether the people running it understand how all three nodes connect, rather than knowing only their own. Not unlike Petit’s concept for Green Berets on long-term Taiwan rotations, a dedicated cadre in this model would instead rotate its personnel sequentially through all three countries, on tours lasting several years each rather than a series of unrelated deployments in which entire teams move in and out at the same time. Optimally, this would include the rotation of not just American advisors but also Japanese, Philippine, and Taiwanese operators. An operator serves a tour in the Philippines, then Japan, then Taiwan, for example, or some ordering suited to the mission, carrying forward what worked in one place and testing it against the next. The result is a body of institutional knowledge about running the resistance pipeline that travels with the people who built it, rather than resetting with every new team that arrives. Foreign Fighters Infiltrate Taiwan to Assist the Resistance (Fictional Image. Image Credit: Google Gemini) Objections Three potential objections to this proposal deserve acknowledgment. The first is consent. Takaichi’s and Marcos’s statements support self-defense and the evacuation of their own nationals. In January 2026, Japan and the Philippines signed a new defense pact amid growing Chinese aggression. Despite this, these actions cannot be interpreted as consent to host an active pipeline built to resupply and reinforce a resistance movement within a state whose government does not formally recognize it. No one should treat public statements from these leaders as a blank check, but the positions from both may serve as a starting point for an expansion of activity. The second is provocation. Beijing’s response to one sentence from Takaichi in the Diet, a halt on Japanese seafood imports , travel advisories, and roughly 500,000 canceled airline tickets , shows how little China needs before retaliating economically. A standing cadre and physical infrastructure on Yonaguni and Batanes will draw an exponentially sharper reaction. The third objection is effectiveness. The Bashi Channel and Miyako Strait are dense, monitored waterways, and unmanned traffic crossing them in wartime will likely be detected and attributed, no matter how careful the tradecraft is, which raises a fair question about whether the pipeline can move enough volume to matter, or perhaps what other functions it may accomplish. Addressing issues related to consent and provocation will be consequential to the success or failure of this proposal. Whether this happens before or after the invasion is also significant. If the Philippines and Japan, or perhaps only one, consider the costs of escalation with China to be borne as a result of embracing this area-complex construct in peacetime, and weigh them against the benefits to be gained for their country in war, they may conclude that the return on investment is worth it. As mentioned earlier, leaders of both countries have articulated that a fight for Taiwan will not be just about Taiwan but will have regional implications, including for their countries. Admittedly, this is not a mitigation of negative costs so much as an acceptance of them. As for the risks associated with establishing communications relay functions and the resistance cadre developing personal relationships on the ground on these adjacent islands, these activities also create similar political and diplomatic costs to those mentioned above. There are genuine, dual-use benefits to establishing communication mechanisms and human-to-human trust networks that come with persistent engagement on these islands, extending beyond conflict or preparation for conflict. Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief preparation, for example, is the most honest example of a capability that would benefit from establishing these systems now. The reality is, however, that building these capabilities prior to invasion may invite retaliation from China. Strategic ambiguity, a constant theme for nearly every country in the world regarding Taiwan, is the first option for the Philippines and Japan as it pursues dual-use preparations discussed here. Or, secondly, both countries may decide to clearly declare their willingness to begin preparing for conflict out of genuine concern for their national security. Or, a third option is that establishing such resistance-support mechanisms may not occur until after hostilities have broken out, and leaders are forced to make hard decisions. The latter outcome doesn’t mean the expanded area complex doesn’t become an operational reality, but it may mean it isn’t optimally planned and exercised. The higher-risk, higher-signature functions involved with the expanded area complex, unmanned insertion runs, and foreign fighter staging become branch plans that would almost certainly not activate until Tokyo or Manila has crossed its own legal thresholds, the same gating already applied to kinetic interdiction. The intent of this paper is not to presuppose what Tokyo or Manila will do or to assume the level of risk these countries are willing to take, but rather to put forth a resistance-support concept and acknowledge the costs associated with it. How these two countries proceed will ultimately be based on what they perceive best for their own survival, not anyone else’s. Effectiveness is a different kind of problem, since it isn’t a matter of managing political risk but of surviving physical detection. There are at least three approaches as to what “success” actually means for this expanded area complex. There is the ambitious one in which the pipeline sustains the resistance movement; the modest one in which the network survives and complicates the enemy’s occupation; and the third, a combination of the two. As for sustaining the resistance itself, it is important to remember that this expanded area complex is the terrestrial-based manifestation of the complex. While the inner and outer zones are where a considerable amount of physical support originates, there will also be maritime (surface and sub-surface), air, space-based, and virtual support to the resistance. Ideally, all of these lines of effort will be well orchestrated. The point here is that it is not only the land-based resistance area complex on Japanese and Philippine islands that will be tasked with supporting the resistance. As for disruption, history provides a useful example. Detachment A, the Cold War Special Forces unit that ran stay-behind operations in West Berlin, never had full deniability, surrounded as it was by Soviet and East German intelligence services, and its value lay in persistence and complication rather than invisibility. This pipeline’s job will include a similar mission: survive attrition and impose cost. In reality, the expanded resistance area complex, together with the other support efforts mentioned, will serve several functions simultaneously. Furthermore, depending on the reality on the ground, one part of the network may serve one function while another serves a different purpose. Summary This paper provides a modern adaptation of the doctrinal “area complex” needed to support resistance on an island facing a realistic threat of invasion and occupation. The overarching strategic concept is outlined here, but the operational and tactical realities of the architecture require additional scrutiny. The idea of a Chinese invasion is often discussed among the US, Taiwan, Japan, the Philippines, and other like-minded partners. The integration of mechanisms across international borders to build depth of resistance to compensate for geographic shortfalls, however, is not explored in practical terms, as it is here. Expanding the area complex’s footprint on the ground is possible if the aperture is spread onto two pieces of partner territory that are not Taiwan’s own.
